title: Configuring and building BALDES
heading: Direct Cargo builds
text:
Direct Cargo builds Install Rust/Cargo and clone the repository. The core library can be builtwithout an external LP backend: cargo build --release
 For the CLI and routing master, initialize the vendored dependencies and buildwith Clp. This requires a C++14 compiler: git submodule update --init vendor/Clp vendor/CoinUtils
cargo build --release --features clp
./target/release/baldes --help
 The clp feature builds Clp 1.17.10 and CoinUtils 2.11 from those submodules.To also enable the optional HiGHS backend and integer solver, install itsshared library and use cargo build --release --features clp,highs.The CLI and routing tree require clp; highs alone provides the library'sHiGHS backend and generic MIP API. See below for library discovery details. Disjoint service-start windows are optional: usecargo build --release --features multi-time-windows for the library, or--features clp,multi-time-windows for network JSON and the CLI. Seemultiple time windows for the Rust,Python and JSON APIs. Python installation is covered in the pybaldes guide.

title: Configuring and building BALDES
heading: Interactive configuration
text:
Interactive configuration From the repository root: make config       # Open the configuration window in your terminal
make              # Compile with the saved settings
 make menuconfig opens the same window. Use Up/Down or J/K to selectan option, Space/Enter to change it, S to save and exit, and Q/Escapeto discard changes. Text fields accept Enter to confirm, Escape to cancel,Backspace to delete and Ctrl-U to clear. Home/End jump to the first/lastsetting; Page Up/Page Down move five settings at a time. Settings are grouped into Build, Performance, Toolchain and Cargo. Wideterminals show contextual help and a live build summary beside the options;compact terminals keep help below the scrolling list. The header tracksunsaved changes. The menu adapts automatically when resized, down to 64 columnsby 20 rows, and respects NO_COLOR for a monochrome display. This is a kernel-style terminal menu, implemented in Rust rather than Linux'sKconfig tooling. It requires Make, Rust/Cargo, and POSIX stty in an interactiveANSI terminal (Linux/macOS). It opens in the current terminal; no desktopsession, Python packages, ncurses headers or UI library downloads are needed.The helper is compiled directly with rustc into target/baldes-build beforeconfiguration, so it does not need to build the solver first.

title: Configuring and building BALDES
heading: Saved settings and automation
text:
Saved settings and automation The menu saves a local .config, ignored by Git. Subsequent Make commandsread it. A missing configuration uses release/library-only defaults with nooptional solver dependencies. Cargo commands invoked directly continue touse their explicit Cargo flags; they do not read .config. make showconfig                # Display effective settings
make print-command             # Preview the Cargo build invocation
make defconfig                 # Replace .config with defaults
make defconfig CONFIG=ci.config # Write another configuration file
make CONFIG=ci.config          # Build with it
 For noninteractive use, run make defconfig and edit the file or supply asaved config via CONFIG=path. The format is CONFIG_NAME=value, using y/nfor booleans and double quotes for strings. Backslashes and quotes in stringsmust be escaped. Missing settings take their defaults; unknown/duplicate keys,invalid values and conflicting dependencies are rejected. The file is parsedas data and is never included as Make code or sourced by a shell. An example configuration for the CLI with both LP backends: CONFIG_PROFILE=release
CONFIG_CLP=y
CONFIG_HIGHS=y
CONFIG_CLI=y
CONFIG_SIMD=off
CONFIG_NATIVE_CPU=n
CONFIG_RELEASE_DEBUG=n
CONFIG_OFFLINE=n
CONFIG_LOCKED=y
CONFIG_JOBS=0
CONFIG_RESOURCE_DIMENSIONS=2
CONFIG_TARGET=""
CONFIG_HIGHS_DIR=""

title: Configuring and building BALDES
heading: Other Make targets
text: Other Make targets Command Action make build / make all Same build as plain make make check Cargo check for the selected artifacts and features make test Run library/integration tests with the selected profile/features make clippy Lint library/integration tests and the selected CLI make fmt Check formatting in the baldes package make clean Run cargo clean -p baldes; retain .config make test-config Test config parsing, dependencies and Cargo argument translation make help List targets and tool overrides make test and make clippy select integration tests as well as the library;Cargo may build the CLI for integration tests when its Clp requirement isenabled, even if the CLI artifact is disabled for ordinary builds. Theworkspace's Python extension is built separately using its existing packagingcommands. CARGO=path and RUSTC=path override the tool executables. Existing compiler/linker environment variables remain available to Cargo.The frontend prints the command and any configuration-specific environmentoverrides before running it and propagates Cargo's failure status to Make. The scalar setting accepts any nonnegative usize. For example,CONFIG_RESOURCE_DIMENSIONS=5 compiles capacity 5; models may activate fewercoordinates. The saved setting overrides BALDES_RESOURCE_DIMENSIONS inheritedfrom the shell for Make builds. Direct Cargo or maturin builds use that environmentvariable instead and do not read .config. Explicit Rust Graph::<D> / Solver::<D>counts remain independent of the configured default. See scalar resources. Optional SIMD is disabled by default. In make config, cycle through off,avx2, and avx512; unsupported CPU modes are skipped. Saved modes are validatedagainst the host CPU and require an empty target triple. Legacy n / y settingsremain accepted as off / avx2.Direct Cargo builds use --features simd for AVX2 or --features simd-avx512for AVX-512F (requires Rust 1.89 or newer). On x86-64, sufficiently longdisposable-resource dominance scans use the selected kernel after runtime CPUdetection. AVX-512 builds fall back to AVX2 when available. Other CPUs and small scans retain theportable implementation. Scalar capacities remain arbitrary; the optimizedscan applies when the model activates one or two disposable resources andthe compiled capacity is at least two.This feature does not require target-cpu=native and does not change numericalcomparison tolerances or certification policy. For eight-label AVX-512F dominance scans, usecargo build --release --features clp,simd-avx512 (or pass the same featuresto maturin). This feature includes simd and requires Rust 1.89 or newer;the default and AVX2-only builds retain the package's existing Rust requirement.Runtime dispatch prefers AVX-512F on supported x86-64 CPUs, then AVX2, thenthe portable implementation. No global CPU flags are required. The AVX-512kernel needs only AVX-512F, including for the packed NG masks, and preservesfirst-candidate ordering and the original floating-point comparison order.See SIMD dispatch for dispatch behavior and portability details.

title: Source layout
heading: Source layout
text: Source layout Production Rust code lives in src/. Unit tests live in tests/unit/, andpublic-interface integration suites live in subsystem directories undertests/. See the test guide for registration andcommands. Runnable demonstrations belong in examples/. Directory Responsibility src/core/ Errors, options, logging, and conservative floating-point arithmetic src/graph/ Graphs, resources, neighborhoods, and bucket construction src/labeling/ Label storage, dominance, and directional labeling engines src/pricing/ Stateful pricing, restrictions, cut preparation, and retained route universes src/enumeration/ Route-domain proofs and bounded path enumeration src/cuts/ Cut families, registration, and shared separation machinery src/master/ LP interfaces, column generation, root solving, branching, and tree search src/master/multi_pricing/ Shared masters with independently priced networks and imported columns src/master/solvers/ Clp and HiGHS backends and shared MIP controls src/extensions/ HGS, IPM, electric-vehicle routing, p-step, and column elimination src/inputs/ Instance parsing and graph construction src/bin/baldes/ Executable entry point and command implementations A module with production child files uses name/mod.rs; a leaf module usesname.rs. This keeps the parent and its implementations together. Rust modulepaths stay independent of these physical filenames. Private implementationmodules group work by responsibility, while the parent defines shared data andexports the public interface. pricing/mod.rs defines the solver state. Construction, configuration, cutpreparation, restriction application, and lifecycle changes have separateimplementations. master/multi_pricing/mod.rs defines its shared model andstate; pricing.rs implements network pricing callbacks, and solve.rsimplements initialization and the solve workflow. Keep test bodies and fixtures outside src/. Attach private unit tests withfeature-gated #[path] module declarations so tests do not require wideningproduction visibility. Keep implementation-specific test adapters gated with#[cfg(test)] when they must access private fields. Extension guides belong indocs/extensions/; dependency licenses remain alongside their implementation.

title: Command-line usage
heading: Command-line usage
text:
Command-line usage Documentation index · Build configuration · Python Commands below run from the repository root after building with --features clp. ./target/release/baldes vrptw instances/R101.txt --customers 25 --rank1
./target/release/baldes cvrp instances/cvrplib/A-n32-k5.vrp --capacity-cuts
./target/release/baldes hgs instances/R101.txt --population-size 50 --nb-iter 5000
 The first argument selects the instance type: vrptw (time windows), cvrp(capacitated, no time windows), or hgs (Hybrid Genetic Search heuristic).The routing commands read Solomon-format files and CVRPLIB (TSPLIB) .vrpfiles; the format is detected from the content. vrptw enforces time windows and service times;cvrp ignores them.CVRPLIB instances have no time windows, so they are solved as cvrp. They usethe file's distance convention: TSPLIB nint for EUC_2D, ceil forCEIL_2D, or the explicit EDGE_WEIGHT_SECTION (full or triangular). As forSolomon files, the root fleet bound is the customer count. Route-length limits (DISTANCE) and service times are not supported. Run./target/release/baldes --help for usage.

title: Command-line usage
heading: Options
text: Options Option Meaning --customers N keep the first N customers --ng N NG neighbourhood size (default 8) --reference-ng the N nearest customers, ties by index (the comparison setup) --rounding MODE distances none, nearest, tenth or ceil (default: the file's convention) --rank1 separate limited-memory rank-one cuts --capacity / --capacity-cuts separate native rounded capacity cuts in the Clp root master --two-path-cuts enable capacity cuts with Kohl's time resource attached (VRPTW only) --tree run branch-and-price for integer routing --nodes N tree node limit (default 10,000) --branching MODE native (default), ryan-foster, vehicles, or arc --no-strong-branching use fractionality instead of phased strong branching --no-diving disable strong diving --no-mip-heuristic disable restricted-master integer search --mip-nodes N node budget per restricted-master integer-search call --enumerated-mip solve complete enumerated node masters with HiGHS; requires --tree and the highs feature --no-enumeration no reduced-cost fixing or enumeration --upper-bound X initial incumbent for fixing --no-stabilization no dual-price smoothing --master MODE clp (default), highs (requires HiGHS), or native ipm; IPM disables stabilization --bound-mode MODE numerical (default) uses pricing bounds with tolerances; certified requires independent original-domain bound validation --hgs-time S positive HGS search budget before routing solve; separate from --time --hgs-columns MODE best plan (default), all distinct feasible routes, or N cheapest new routes --dynamic-ng P strengthen NG memories from master cycles at separator priority P --option NAME=VALUE set a supported BALDES pricing option (repeatable) --verbose, -v, --log solver progress table on stderr, every 10 CG iterations --log-interval N enable progress every N CG iterations; N must be positive --iterations N master iteration limit --time S routing solve or standalone HGS time limit in seconds --json FILE write root LP/history or HGS solution results --population-size N HGS minimum population size (default: 25) --nb-iter N HGS iterations without improvement before stopping/restarting --seed N HGS random seed (default: 0) --help, -h show all CLI options, including tree controls Root Optimal means the LP relaxation converged; tree Optimal means theinteger routing gap closed within the configured tolerances. HGS suppliesfeasible solutions without an optimality proof. Root LP route values can befractional, and NG routes can revisit customers. Normal root and tree solves use numerical bounds and skip the full certificatesearch. Use --bound-mode certified for independently validated bounds. Thatmode attempts validation when an exact pass can close pricing or the incumbentgap; failure leaves its selected bound unknown. Route-feasibility checks andexact pricing remain enabled in both modes. JSON reports bound_mode, the selected bound, and separate numerical_boundand certified_bound fields. An unknown bound is null. A numerical estimatenever substitutes for an unknown certified bound. A tree result labels theguarantee of its global bound; it does not report a global numerical estimatein certified mode. Root results retain both estimates when available. Solomon instances are in instances/, and a few CVRPLIB ones ininstances/cvrplib/. Enable --verbose for an aligned progress table with the restricted-masterobjective, selected lower bound, incumbent, gap, reduced cost, column counts,pricing phase, and elapsed time. Use --log-interval 5 for more frequent output.When cut families are enabled, the table also shows their current cut counts;disabled families have no column. For advanced routing, see the branch-and-price tree guide andenumerated MIP guide. Build instructions are in the build guide; benchmark results are inRoot benchmarks. For named pricing controls, see the BALDES option reference.Public option names start with BALDES, for example--option BALDESlabelDominanceStrategy=1. Rust exposes supported metadata inOPTION_TABLE; Python exposes Solver.option_names() andSolver.option_support(name). The public list contains 39 supported controls,plus two enumerated-MIP controls when both clp and highs are enabled.Scope can depend on the operation or configured cut family.

title: Python: pybaldes
heading: Python: pybaldes
text:
Python: pybaldes Documentation index · Command-line usage Commands below run from the repository root. Python 3.9+, Rust/Cargo and aC++14 compiler are required to build the default package from source. The Python distribution and import are both named pybaldes. It contains thelow-level Solver, Route, and Phase bindings and direct Rust-backed VRPTW/CVRProot solving. The default build includes the Clp master, built from the samevendor/ submodules as the Rust CLI: git submodule update --init
python -m pip install .
 import pybaldes

result = pybaldes.solve_root(
    "instances/R101.txt",
    problem_type="vrptw",  # or "cvrp" for CVRPLIB .vrp files
    customers=25,
    capacity_cuts=True,
    rank_one_cuts=True,
    time_limit=120,
)
print(result.status, result.lp, result.bound, result.cuts)
for route in result.routes:
    print(route.value, route.cost, route.nodes)
 Instance.from_file(path) reads Solomon-format and CVRPLIB .vrp files. You can also build inputsin memory: from pybaldes import Customer, Instance

instance = Instance("small", capacity=2, customers=[
    Customer(0, 0),  # depot, zero demand
    Customer(1, 0, demand=1),
    Customer(0, 1, demand=1),
])
result = instance.solve_root(problem_type="cvrp", capacity_cuts=True)
 CVRP ignores time windows and service times; in-memory VRPTW data requires finiteready/due windows, including the depot. vehicles is retained as inputmetadata; the current root model uses the customer count as its fleet upperbound, matching the Rust CLI.

title: Python: pybaldes
heading: Solve options and results
text:
Solve options and results Options include ng, reference_ng, rounding (none, nearest, tenth, ceil),stabilize, reduced_cost_fixing, upper_bound, max_iterations,max_cut_rounds, and a pricing_options dictionary of BALDES option values.Disabling reduced-cost fixing also disables enumeration. Results include positiveLP routes, duals, iteration history, cut/fixing counts, and timers;result.to_dict() and result.to_json() export them. to_dict() retainsinfinite values; to_json() converts non-finite values to null.Cut counts include generated rows later retired.These are root LP relaxations; Optimal does not certify an integer VRP optimum. Option Default Meaning master_solver "clp" Select "clp", native "ipm", or "highs" (requires its build feature); IPM disables stabilization bound_mode "numerical" Use numerical pricing bounds, or "certified" for independent original-domain bound validation verbose False Print column-generation progress to stderr log_interval 10 Positive iteration interval for progress when verbose hgs_time None Positive HGS search budget in seconds before the root solve, separate from time_limit hgs_columns "best" Seed the best plan, "all" validated encountered routes, or a positive integer of cheapest new routes hgs_seed 0 Random seed for HGS seeding result.bound_mode identifies the selected result.bound guarantee.result.numerical_bound and result.certified_bound are separate: unknowncertificates remain negative infinity (null in JSON), even when a numericalestimate is finite. Normal mode skips certificate searches; exact pricing androute-feasibility validation remain enabled. Certified mode requests a boundwhen pricing or the incumbent gap may close. Failure never promotes thenumerical estimate to a certificate. For example, seed a native IPM root solve with HGS and log progress: result = pybaldes.solve_root(
    "instances/R101.txt", customers=25,
    master_solver="ipm", hgs_time=2, hgs_columns="all", verbose=True,
)
print(result.to_json())
 Python root solves enable Kohl with two_path_cuts=True. This attaches timeresource 0 for capacity-cut registration;ordinary capacity cuts retain the default resource -1. Both use the capacityfamily's priority 3 at root and 1 below it, complement form and persistent subset pool.

text: Branch-and-price tree and node lifecycle Documentation index · Branching ·Enumerated MIP The Rust tree solves a routing set-partitioning master with one pricing graph.It requires nonnegative arc costs and unique public arc IDs. The base rows area fleet upper bound and one equality per customer; the tree validates thisstructure before searching.

title: Branch-and-price tree and node lifecycle
heading: Node processing
text: Node processing The search selects a node by its lower bound and evaluates it within theremaining global budget. Its main steps are: Construct the root master, or fork the solved parent and append the child'sconstraints. Run column generation, pricing, cut rounds, and enabled fixing/enumeration. Share valid elementary routes with the incumbent heuristic and other nodes. Search restricted columns for a feasible integer solution; optionally runHiGHS over a complete enumerated universe. Close the node when its selected bound meets the incumbent gap, or selecta branching candidate and create children. Strong trials and diving useisolated evaluations. Time limits are cooperative across solver operations. A backend call canfinish after its requested budget. Limits preserve bounds for unfinished nodes. options.root.bound_mode selects BoundMode::Numerical by default, orBoundMode::Certified for independent original-domain validation. The CLIequivalent is --bound-mode numerical|certified. Numerical bounds authorizeordinary pruning within the configured tolerances. Certified mode never usesa numerical estimate to close a node: an unsuccessful certificate attemptleaves the bound unknown. TreeOutput::bound_mode and JSON label the boundand the guarantee of gap-based termination. Warm starts retain the two boundsseparately, so changing modes cannot promote a parent's numerical estimate.

title: Branch-and-price tree and node lifecycle
heading: What a child inherits
text: What a child inherits State Child handling Clp master Deep-copy model, basis, solution, scaling, and simplex state Branch and cut rows Preserve physical rows and coefficient mappings; append new branch rows Existing route columns Retain coefficients and upper bounds; retire routes outside the new domain Pricing graph Carry bucket preparation, fixed bucket arcs, NG state, options, and adaptive state Labels Rebuild for the child's duals and active branch resources Enumeration Retain/filter routes where compatible and preserve branch-distinct arc paths Sibling state Own independent mutable models and pricing state When enumeration changes the master to full-memory cut coefficients, existingcolumns are updated as well as new ones. Reusing limited-memory coefficientsfor only part of the enumerated master would change the model.

title: Branch-and-price tree and node lifecycle
heading: Root snapshots and manual inheritance
text: Root snapshots and manual inheritance Set RootOptions::capture_state = true to retain a solved NodeSnapshot inRootOutput::snapshot. The tree arranges snapshot capture for its own nodes.Manual callers use root::inherit_branches(parent, additional_branches, options)for typed constraints, or root::inherit for arc-flow tuples. Supply only theadditional branches; the parent already contains its ancestor rows.To retain the child's snapshot for another generation, enable capture on thatsolve too. Snapshots retain both restricted-master columns and the generated column pool,including cached columns that have not entered the master. Child branch rowsand cut cleanup update cached coefficients as well as loaded coefficients.Regeneration checks the child's current path restrictions; a cached route isnot automatically admissible. Manually constructed column-generationWarmStart values provide generated_pool in creation order; an empty pool isinitialized from the loaded columns. The snapshot exposes bound_mode(), branch_depth(), active_cuts(), andenumerated_routes(). A route count alone does not establish completeness;the enumerated-MIP adapter separately checks the completion flag.

title: Branch-and-price tree and node lifecycle
heading: Incumbents, proofs, and status
text: Incumbents, proofs, and status Source Supplies an incumbent? Certifies the routing lower bound? Validated elementary route solution Yes No, by its objective alone Restricted-column integer heuristic Yes, after validation No Exact node pricing When the resulting routes form an integer witness Numerical estimate in normal mode; independent certificate required in certified mode Heuristic strong trial or dive Can find a witness No proof for the original node Complete enumerated HiGHS MIP Yes, after validation Only within saved enumeration coverage and for proved outcomes A cost-only --upper-bound can assist root fixing, but the tree needs actualfeasible routes before accepting an incumbent. It does not invent a solutionfrom the supplied number. Optimal means the configured numerical gap is closed. TimeLimit,NodeLimit, and Incomplete retain unfinished-node bounds. Check whether afinite incumbent and routes are present before treating a limited run as asolution. JSON encodes nonfinite numbers as null. The restricted-column heuristic uses TreeOptions::mip_node_limit andmip_time_limit; CLI --mip-nodes budgets that heuristic. Optional HiGHS nodeMIP has separate controls and counters; see Enumerated MIP.

title: Branch-and-price tree and node lifecycle
heading: Limits and supported models
text: Limits and supported models Every root, child, and priced trial runs node preprocessing before columngeneration. A worklist propagates continuous bounds through the originalarc-flow master rows and flow conservation, including equivalent outgoingcover rows. Child nodes also propagate active inherited capacity, complement,and two-path cut rows using their exact additive arc coefficients and currentphysical row bounds. Retired cut rows are excluded. Contradictions certify node infeasibility without LP solving orpricing. Zero upper bounds retire inherited columns and restrict both pricingdirections and complete enumeration. Positive aggregate lower bounds remainenforced by their original master rows; they do not require every route tocontain the arc. Parent and sibling state remains independent. RootOutput::preprocessing reports bound updates, processed rows,infeasibility, and whether the bounded worklist reached completion. Reachingthe work limit keeps valid deductions and continues ordinary node evaluation.The reusable master::preprocessing engine accepts signed sparse rows andinfinite variable bounds, but callers must supply a complete formulation.Applying it to an unfinished restricted-column master would be unsound. Ryan–Foster preprocessing closes transitive together groups, excludes arcsbetween apart groups, and fixes all incident arcs of an internally contradictorygroup to zero. Covering and assignment rows then determine whether that groupis mandatory and the node is infeasible. Pricing resources still enforce thecomplete route-level rules; preprocessing does not replace them. Preprocessing currently covers the single-network routing model. The boundedactivity worklist may leave contradictions that require solving the LP.Decomposition-wide local/global multiplicity links remain outside this adapter.

title: Routing branching
heading: Routing branching
text: Routing branching Documentation index · Tree lifecycle The tree branches on aggregate route quantities. Each child receives a typedconstraint, inherited master rows, and a compatible pricing domain. Thestandard routing model uses customer vertices as packing sets and enforcesunit customer coverage with equality rows.

title: Routing branching
heading: Choosing families
text:
Choosing families CLI mode Candidate families, in priority order --branching native (default) Vehicle count, packing-set assignment, Ryan–Foster, arc flow --branching vehicles Vehicle count, then arc-flow fallback --branching ryan-foster Ryan–Foster, then arc-flow fallback --branching arc Arc flow --branching cluster Cluster boundary/pair variables, then arc-flow fallback --branching resource Accumulated-resource splits, then arc-flow fallback --branching hybrid Vehicle count, resource/cluster, assignment, Ryan–Foster, arc flow The default selector visits enabled families in descending model priority. Withinan applicable family it orders candidates by closeness of the fractional partto 0.5, with stable ties. Phased strong branching then evaluates candidateswhen enabled. These are adapter priorities, not a combined ranking across allfamilies. Families in the same integer priority group can contribute together.Rust callers can set BranchingOptions::priorities; its defaults are vehiclecount 11, resource/cluster 10, assignment 3, Ryan–Foster 2 and arc flow 1.These are Baldes adapter settings; reference model interfaces also registerpriorities explicitly. Every supplied priority must be finite. cargo run --release --features clp --bin baldes -- \
  vrptw instances/R101.txt --customers 10 --tree \
  --branching ryan-foster --time 60
 Rust configures the family flags through TreeOptions::branching, whose typeis BranchingOptions. Arc flow remains the fallback when all flags are false.

title: Routing branching
heading: Number of vehicles
text:
Number of vehicles Let v be the sum of LP values of nonempty routes in the selected network.For fractional v, the children enforce: down: number of nonempty routes <= floor(v)
up:   number of nonempty routes >= ceil(v)
 Pricing receives this row through nonempty-route return arcs to the sink.The split-depot source-to-sink arc contributes zero to this branch. Theoriginal fleet upper bound remains in the master.

title: Routing branching
heading: Ryan–Foster
text: Ryan–Foster For customers i and j, let w(i,j) be the sum of LP route values for routesvisiting both customers. When 0 < w(i,j) < 1, the children require: Child Allowed routes Apart A route can visit at most one of the pair Together A route visits both customers or neither Both children work with a single pricing network. The together conditionapplies to each route, rather than merely requiring both customers somewherein the final solution. Binary resources enforce the rule during labeling and bidirectional joins.Retained enumeration is filtered by the same rule. Existing NG routes thatrepeat a pair endpoint are retired from the child master. A violation row alsokeeps inherited and newly added master columns consistent with the branch. An apart constraint consumes one binary resource; a together constraintconsumes three. The current representation holds 512 resources. Candidategeneration skips already-branched pairs and falls back to arc flow when itcannot reserve resources for both Ryan–Foster children.

title: Routing branching
heading: Packing-set assignment
text: Packing-set assignment This family branches on assigning a customer packing set to a particularpricing network. If its fractional assignment to network k is y, thechildren enforce assignment to that network as zero or at least one.For example, in a heterogeneous fleet this could decide whether customer 7uses the small-vehicle network. The current tree has one network. Its customer equality rows already fixeach assignment to one. Assignment constraints can be constructed and enforced,but the normal single-network LP has no fractional assignment candidate. Anunassigned child for a mandatory customer is infeasible. Useful assignment branching requires multiple route families/networks,network-specific costs and resources, and master columns carrying the networkidentity. Setting a graph ID alone does not add that modeling support.

title: Routing branching
heading: Directed arc flow
text: Directed arc flow For a directed arc with fractional LP usage f, the children enforce flow atmost floor(f) or at least ceil(f). Route coefficients count traversals ofthe arc; branch duals also reach pricing through that arc. BranchConstraint::ArcFlow::arc takes the arc's position inproblem.graph.arcs, while Route::arcs stores public arc IDs. UseRootProblem::arc_position(id) to convert an ID to a position.

title: Routing branching
heading: Strong branching and diving
text: Strong branching and diving Strong branching is enabled by default. Its three phases retain up to 100restricted-LP candidates, price three survivors heuristically, then evaluateone with exact pricing. An intermediate restricted-LP or heuristic phase isskipped when all remaining candidates fit in the next phase. Terminal phasesstill run their trials, including explicitly heuristic-only configurations.Each Rust StrongPhase also has a subtree_ratio: positive values limitbranching work using the estimated remaining subtree size; zero disables thatphase's adaptive limit. The defaults are 0.3, 0.1 and 1. Moving below theparent's stored branch-family priority cutoff restores the full fresh quota.These estimates schedule trials and never strengthen a pruning bound. TheReliable comparison policy retains its fixed budgets.Rust callers can enable StrongBranchingOptions::use_history_subtree_size toprefer completed subtree sizes at the current depth. Until that depth has anobservation, the parent estimate remains the fallback. Partial or interruptedsubtrees do not enter this average. The default keeps parent estimates.StrongBranchingOptions exposes the phase and timebudgets. Disable it with --no-strong-branching. Strong round-up diving uses isolated route-fixing trials and depth,discrepancy, node, and time limits. Disable it with --no-diving.Heuristic trial objectives and dive bounds cannot certify the original node.See Tree lifecycle for bound and incumbent handling.

title: Routing branching
heading: Cluster branching
text: Cluster branching --branching cluster enables the cluster variables of Silva, Uchoa andSubramanian, Cluster Branching for Vehicle Routing Problems (2024),Sections 3 and 4.1. For a customer cluster C, the boundary variable countsentries from outside C, equivalent to half the undirected cutset flow on acomplete depot-to-depot route. For disjoint clusters C,D, the pair variablecounts arc traversals in either direction between them. Both variables areinteger in an integer routing solution. Children impose floor/ceiling boundson their fractional LP values. The split source/sink form one depot cluster. Coefficients are additive over physical arcs, including repeated crossings.Branch duals therefore use the existing arc-cost pricing path, without extralabel resources. Arc-flow candidates remain available because clustervariables alone do not ensure an integral directed solution. ClusterBranchingOptions::partition accepts a partition of every customerexactly once. Otherwise a deterministic customer MST is cut at edges strictlyabove mean + theta * standard_deviation; theta defaults to 1. Distances usethe cheaper physical arc in either direction. This matches geometric distanceson symmetric routing graphs; for asymmetric/sparse graphs it is a heuristicsimilarity measure. A disconnected customer graph supplies no automaticcustomer clusters. The partition is constructed once per tree. Other clusteringmethods and the paper's full computational experiment are not implemented.

title: Routing branching
heading: Accumulated-resource branching
text: Accumulated-resource branching --branching resource adds schedule candidates, retaining arc-flow fallback.An individual constraint identifies a public arc ID, a resource coordinate, a threshold,and a side. threshold is stored with an offset: the effective boundary isthreshold - 1e-6. It restricts the resource at that arc's head after consumptionand waiting to <= boundary or >= boundary. Equality belongs to both children;there is no gap between their schedule domains. This is a continuous resourcesplit, not a floor/ceiling split of the resource value. Other routes need notuse the selected arc. An empty window intersection forbids that arc. The implementation tightens the physical arc's resource window. Existingforward/backward extensions, resource replay and enumeration enforce it.Inherited columns also receive a nonnegative violation row, so an old schedulecannot satisfy the new master solely because its arc path is still present.Resource-domain changes discard inherited labels/enumeration before repricing;parent and sibling graphs remain independent. Original resource limits remainin effect. The existing requirement for backward equality resources to have afixed sink window still applies. Automatic candidates group all arcs entering a covered customer, backed by itsunit packing row. For disposable resources, they combine forward head quantitieswith backward feasible suffix upper bounds, including ancestor resource windows.A tolerance-merged weighted event walk selects an endpoint threshold;overlapping intervals can supply no useful split even when forward quantitiesdiffer. The event kernel is checked against 839 native separator cases. Ordinaryfractional arcs retain arc-flow candidates; no speed improvement or completenative child-workflow equivalence is claimed. Rust master callers can construct AccumulatedResourceGroupBranch with a backingpacking-row index and unique physical arc IDs. The row must have upper RHS atmost one and nonnegative coefficients, with each member arc contributing at leastone. This proves at most one group occurrence in an integer solution; arbitraryarc sets do not define a valid binary disjunction. Nonempty member windows aretightened together. Empty member windows contribute zero-flow enforcement forthose arcs, while other members remain available. Parent and sibling statesstay independent. Complete enumeration retains distinct physical paths even when their packingsupport is identical. A costlier path can have a different resource profileand remain necessary after fixing routes or applying a descendant restriction. The Rust pricing API exposes AccumulatedResourceBranch, its boundary() and satisfied_by()methods, and the add/clear methods on Solver. To request a split near resource value t, passthreshold = t + 1e-6; boundary() reports the actual floating-point split.Older builds used the supplied threshold directly. Existing callers that needto preserve their split must account for the offset when upgrading. --branching hybrid enables both new families alongside the native families.Vehicle count keeps its first default priority. Resource/cluster candidatesshare the next priority; assignment, Ryan–Foster and arc flow remain fallbacks.native remains the default, with both new families disabled.

title: Routing branching
heading: Branch evaluation history
text:
Branch evaluation history Tree search enables branch evaluation history by default, using the recoverednative ranking rules. No extra flag is required. --no-branch-history disablesrecording and history-based ranking; --branch-history explicitly enables themagain. The last flag wins. TreeOutput::branch_history records finite strong-trial and completed nodeevaluations, exported as branch_evaluations in JSON. Each record identifiesthe constraint, depth, evaluation kind, one-based evaluation stage (stage), parent bound, child estimate, fractionaldistance and elapsed time. Restricted-master, heuristic-pricing, exact-pricingand ordinary-node observations remain separately identified. Ordinary nodes havestage: null; they contribute to the Rust Reliable comparison policy but notthe default strong-phase ranking. Unfinished exact trials andsentinel/infinite estimates do not supply observations. Restricted-masterestimates can include artificial penalties. For each constraint and child direction, history averages signed objective gaindivided by branching distance. It uses the latest local stage with either childobserved; an unobserved child has mean zero. Each predicted child gain is cappedby the incumbent-minus-parent gap, and their product supplies the score.Candidates are ordered by stage, then decreasing score, then lexical generatorlabel. Resource groups use ES_<packing_row>_rID_<resource>_<threshold>, withthe stored threshold displayed to six significant digits. Other families usecanonical constraint names. Negative gains are retained and there is no positive scorefloor. At non-root nodes, half of the first strong-branching phase's budget is reservedfor history. Fresh generation stops before a lower integer priority group onceit has candidates, or when its quota fills. The stopping priority determineswhich stored generators can enter history ranking. Enabled empty families stillaffect this cutoff. Admission happens before stored activity is replayed; a highhistorical score cannot bypass it. The remainder retains fresh candidate order. Without strongtrials, history can still rank candidates. History starts empty for each solveand never supplies a pruning bound or marks a node infeasible. With accumulated-resource branching enabled, the default policy also retainsevaluated group thresholds and refreshes their fractional activity at laternodes. An older threshold can enter history selection even when fresh separationchooses another threshold for that group. Evaluated arc, vehicle, assignment,Ryan–Foster and cluster generators also refresh under their enabled familypriorities; numeric bounds are rebuilt around the current activity. Already applied splits, integralactivities and groups without a valid packing proof are excluded. The recordedresource activity is the route mass strictly below the threshold boundary;down/up history distances are that activity and its complement. The default policy indexes observations by the number of evaluations actuallyrun on that candidate side at the current node, independently of whether atrial uses restricted-master, heuristic or exact pricing. Skipped phases consumeno stage; an exact trial after skipped ranking phases is stage one. The Reliable policy keepssemantic evaluation kinds separate and retains the earlier adapter selectionworkflow for controlled comparisons. Custom priority scheduling applies to thedefault policy. Exact resource split identities remaindistinct even when rounded display labels coincide. Rust adapters can registeroriginal model names with branching.generator_names.insert(&constraint, name).Registering either side names both sides of that exact generator. Display namesonly resolve equal-score ties and never merge histories; unnamed generatorsretain canonical labels. Automatic name mapping across native model interfacesremains unverified, soidentical native candidate selection is not guaranteed. No speed improvementis claimed. Rust defaults select BranchHistoryPolicy::ObservedNative inBranchHistoryOptions. Per-network route-count branches remain fresh candidates;this policy excludes them from stored-history ranking and generator replay.Their trial measurements remain available in diagnostics. The earlier Reliable policy remains available throughRust for controlled comparisons: it requires minimum_observations on bothsides, clamps negative gains, uses uncapped predictions with positive floors,and preserves supplied order on ties. minimum_observations does not affectthe default observed-native policy. Set TreeOptions::branch_history to Noneto disable history. The public score_with_gap method accepts the currentincumbent-minus-parent gap. cargo run --release --features clp --bin baldes -- \
  vrptw instances/R101.txt --customers 10 --tree \
  --branching hybrid --time 60 --json /tmp/tree.json

title: Routing cuts
heading: Strong k-path adapters
text: Strong k-path adapters KPathCutConfig::new(demands, capacity) is the routing convenience adapter.Its demand vector uses depot index 0 and customer indices 1..n; the splitsink is n + 1. with_time_windows supplies optional time-window data. NativeKPathCutConfig accepts explicit graphs, graph IDs, packing/coveringset incidence, and demands in the original zero-based set order without adepot entry. Use it when the convenience adapter does not represent the inputmapping. with_kpath_cuts and with_native_kpath_cuts select alternativeadapters; the most recently selected one replaces the other. Graph IDs, set IDs, and pricing vertex indices have different roles. Keepthose mappings explicit when registering cuts. Full-memory enumeration andlimited-memory pricing can use different coefficient state; the adapterupdates the master when switching modes.

title: Routing cuts
heading: Route-load knapsack and resource IDs
text: Route-load knapsack and resource IDs KnapsackCutConfig::new(rows) takes integer resource rows fromcuts::knapsack::KnapsackRow. Separation uses route resource loads, andpricing must charge the same load-dependent contribution. Ordinary arc-onlycosts are insufficient for this family. KnapsackCutConfig::with_resource_indices(map) maps resource IDs in thoserows to coordinates in the pricing solver. An empty map uses identitymapping. For example, an input resource identified as 7 can map to solvercoordinate 1. This changes the coordinate lookup, while preserving resourceIDs in the cut associations. The mapping must remain valid through pricing,enumeration, and child inheritance. Keep rows integer-scaled according to their model semantics. The resourcemap is not a unit conversion. See the mapped-resource and load-dependentpricing cases in the integration tests forcomplete fixtures. For direct Rust pricing::Solver use, setknapsack_exact_coefficients = true to evaluate graph-scaled coefficients withunrounded nonpositive master duals. The setting survives fork_for_node() andapplies to pricing and enumeration. It rejects positive duals and non-monotonestep tables. This option does not turn numerical route costs into directedcertificates or automatically register shared-network rows. The default retainsthe existing rounded pricing convention.

title: Routing cuts
heading: Fenchel separation
text:
Fenchel separation cargo run --release --features clp --bin baldes -- \
  cvrp instances/cvrplib/E-n22-k4.vrp --fenchel-cuts --time 30
 The CVRP/VRPTW switch builds an integer load row from total customer demand,divides demands by their greatest common divisor, and enables Fenchel alone.Demands must be nonnegative integers. The normalized total must not exceed4096; use explicit Rust resource rows and limits for larger domains.Instance::fenchel_cut_config() exposes the same configuration to Rust. For custom rows, use KnapsackCutConfig::new(rows).with_fenchel(parameters),where parameters is cuts::knapsack::FenchelParameters. This builder retainsthe configured rounding/1K families. Each supplied row must be a valid integerpacking inequality on additive, nonnegative route loads. An auxiliary CLP model solves the dual of the recovered bin-packing coveringformulation; unbounded-knapsack dynamic programming generates pattern constraints.Extraction waits for auxiliary convergence. Before returning a cut,integer-profit dynamic programming certifies its integer coefficients and RHS.The monotone step extension also covers loads absent from the current master.Fenchel cuts automatically use graph-scaled coefficients and unrounded dualsin pricing and enumeration, including child solvers and integer transfer. Defaults limit separation to 128 load types, 128 LP iterations, and two secondsper separation call. A limit or failure to find a representable violated cutdoes not certify membership in the integer hull. Separation is opt-in andrequires clp.

title: Routing cuts
heading: Configuration boundaries
text: Configuration boundaries Named BALDES options do not create model data. Enabling capacity separationstill requires demands and vehicle capacity; setting a knapsack mode stillrequires resource rows. Explicit capacity enablement and per-round overridesare applied after inherited cut state is installed. Knapsack constructionoverrides do not reconfigure an existing inherited separator. See BALDES options for supported values and setter errors.

title: Routing cuts
heading: Pricing, enumeration, and integer solving
text: Pricing, enumeration, and integer solving Separation creates rows and registers their pricing state. Pricing incorporates active cut duals while constructing routes. Complete elementary enumeration uses full-memory coefficients, includingupdates to route columns already in the master. Child snapshots preserve active rows and cut state. The optionalHiGHS solve rebuilds full-memory route columns againstevery active physical row and omits artificial columns.

title: Routing cuts
heading: Presence-based costs in the labeling engine
text: Presence-based costs in the labeling engine The low-level Rust LabelingEngine::load_presence(graph, rows) interface acceptscuts::soft_conflicts::PricingInput descriptors. Each contains a PresenceRow,a dual, and one event list per physical arc in graph.arcs order. Eventsidentify original variables: several arcs can emit the same event, and an arccan emit several events. Repeated visits emit presence once. Mode::PairCount counts stored pairs whose two events occur on a route;Mode::AnyPair charges at most once across the entire row. Duplicate pairscount separately in pair-count mode. The engine subtracts dual times thecoefficient from route cost; original_cost retains physical arc costs.Duals are unrounded. Invalid mappings, nonfinite duals or costs outside theengine's supported finite arithmetic range return an error without replacingits previous preparation. Presence incidence participates in dominance, forward/backward joins, completionbounds and reduced-cost fixing. Symmetric prefix reuse switches to ordinarybidirectional labeling to preserve physical event orientation. Installing orclearing rows invalidates cached labels; pass an empty list to clear them. For stateful pricing, use pricing::Solver::set_presence_rows(rows) and inspectits descriptors with presence_rows(). The solver owns these rows acrossengine rebuilds, node forks and raw variable-cost pricing. Changed rows or dualsinvalidate cost-dependent labels, bucket fixing and retained enumeration;identical inputs retain working state. Validation failures preserve the priorrows and caches. Logical branches and physical arc exclusions remain in force.Pass an empty list to clear the rows. These interfaces cover pricing, fixing, enumeration and retained-path repricing.Enumeration preserves distinct physical arc paths when presence rows are active,so different variable incidence cannot merge through customer-set equivalence.It follows the configured cutoff, route and work limits; a failed attempt doesnot publish a partial universe. Presence costs are replayed when retained pathsare inspected or priced, including in node forks. Symmetric physical graphs useordinary directional buckets for these rows. Use the solver setter to keep owned descriptors and engine costs consistent.Enumeration rejects conflicting rows installed only on its engine. Rust callersconstructing enumeration::Label or CutTables literals should initialize thenew presence fields to None for models without presence rows. Shared-master row registration remains under development. These numericalpricing costs do not by themselves publish a certified master bound.

title: Dual-price stabilization
heading: Dual-price stabilization
text: Dual-price stabilization Documentation index · Tree lifecycle Column generation can repeatedly produce similar master duals and columns.BALDES optionally smooths the dual point sent to pricing, using a storedcenter and bounded retries when smoothed pricing finds no fresh columns.It is enabled by default in column_generation::Options. The implementation isDualPriceSmoothing, integrated by thecolumn-generation loop. The sections belowdescribe the implemented update and retry rules.

title: Dual-price stabilization
heading: Smoothing weight
text:
Smoothing weight For raw master duals raw, stored center, and an outward point outward: pricing[i] = (1 - effective_alpha) * outward[i]
           + effective_alpha * center[i]
 By default outward = raw. Larger alpha means more weight on the center.At alpha zero pricing uses the outward point; at alpha one it uses the center.Reducing alpha moves pricing back toward the current master duals. After interpolation, a positive dual on a LessEqual row or a negative dualon a GreaterEqual row is set to zero when its magnitude exceeds theconfigured tolerance. Equality rows have no such sign restriction.

title: Dual-price stabilization
heading: Parameters
text: Parameters These are Rust master::stabilization::Parameters, configured throughRootOptions::cg.smoothing or directly in column_generation::Options.They are separate from the named BALDES pricing options. Parameter Default Behavior alpha_factor 1.0 Below 1: use that base alpha and the linear retry rule; otherwise adapt alpha dynamically initial_alpha 0.5 Initial base alpha for the dynamic mode beta_factor 0.0 Zero: use raw outward point; positive: enable the directional construction below max_updates 10 Maximum smoothed retry updates before returning to raw duals min_gap 0.0 Minimum accepted gap, using the comparison tolerance max_gap 0.0 Maximum accepted gap; nonpositive disables the upper gate minimum_stage 0 Minimum stage accepted by after_master tolerance 1e-6 General comparison and sign-correction tolerance The reference stores alpha_factor, beta_factor, min_gap and max_gapas single-precision controls. The constructor rounds these fields through f32before using them as f64. A factor that rounds to zero disables stabilization. The column-generation caller passes the current pricing stage. Its gap comparesthe inherited node lower bound with the best artificial-free restricted-LPobjective accepted before this solve, using the reference comparison tolerance.It tracks these separately from the global integer incumbent. A new cut orenumeration round carries the certified lower bound and resets the LP bound.Unknown bounds use finite -1e12/+1e12 sentinels; a known lower bound with anunknown LP bound therefore gives a gap slightly below one. Warm starts retainthe parent certificate.

title: Dual-price stabilization
heading: Lifecycle
text: Lifecycle Method Effect restart_schedule(phase) Reset base/effective alpha, retry count, active flag, and center phase; retain the stored center/bound vectors after_master(...) Apply a pending center, store raw duals/senses, reset retries, and activate smoothing if the stage/gap/alpha gates allow it after_pricing(feedback) Consider a center update, adjust base alpha, and decide whether pricing should retry after_iteration() Clear the moved-center marker and return active pricing to raw duals remap_rows(map) Compact dual, center, sense, and pending-center vectors after row removal The first master iteration uses raw duals. Cut/enumeration transitions restartthe schedule; row cleanup applies the row map. Removing columns alone doesnot change row coordinates and does not require a center remap.

title: Dual-price stabilization
heading: Pricing retries and alpha updates
text:
Pricing retries and alpha updates Feedback includes the fresh negative-column count, a subgradient vector,Lagrangian value, and pricing phase. In the column-generation driver, thesubgradient starts at the row RHS and subtracts multiplicity times the bestreturned acceptable column's coefficients. A near-zero or rounded-zero reducedcost does not suppress this contribution. On the first pricing pass in dynamic mode (alpha_factor >= 1): if no fresh negative columns or angle > 1e-12:
    alpha -= 0.1
else if angle < -1e-12 and alpha is below the near-one gate:
    alpha += 0.1 * (1 - alpha)
 The angle threshold is 1e-12, independently of Parameters::tolerance.The near-one gate includes the general tolerance and a relative margin.Updating base alpha affects subsequent master iterations; retries update thecurrent effective alpha separately. The angle is calculated only on that firstadaptive pricing pass and retained during subsequent mispricing retries. If fresh negative columns exist, or smoothing is inactive, after_pricingreturns false and stops retrying. Otherwise it increments misprices and uses: dynamic mode: effective_alpha = 1 - 2 * (1 - effective_alpha)
fixed-base mode: effective_alpha = 1 - misprices * (1 - alpha)
 It republishes a smoothed point only while the retry count is at mostmax_updates and effective alpha exceeds the tolerance. When either gatefails, it deactivates smoothing and requests a final retry at raw duals.“Fixed” describes the base alpha, not an unchanging effective retry weight.The dynamic formula preserves the compiled reference's floating-point operationorder; rewriting it as 2 * effective_alpha - 1 can change the result.

title: Dual-price stabilization
heading: Center updates
text:
Center updates A nonfinite Lagrangian value is ignored. If the current center phase is lessthan or equal to the feedback phase, a finite center bound is replaced onlywhen the new value improves it beyond tolerance. A lower-numbered feedbackphase can reset the center phase and accept a different bound without thatsame improvement requirement. The accepted pricing point and feedback subgradient become a pendingcenter, installed by the next after_master call. Consequently the storedcenter bound is not unconditionally monotone across phase changes. The angle helper computes: toward = pricing - center
angle = dot(toward, feedback_subgradient)
      / (norm(toward) * norm(feedback_subgradient))
 The division is unguarded. A zero denominator may yield NaN; comparisonswith it then fail. This behavior differs from forcing an angle of zero.

title: Dual-price stabilization
heading: Optional directional construction
text:
Optional directional construction With positive beta_factor, let d = raw - center, l = norm(d), and gbe the stored normalized center subgradient. A negligible l returns raw duals.For beta_factor == 1, beta is the cosine between d and g; a negligiblesubgradient also returns raw duals. Otherwise the configured beta is used.Beta is clamped to [0, 1] before constructing: outward = center + (1 - beta) * d + beta * l * g
 A negligible subgradient contributes zero to its directional term. When theconstructed step has norm above 1e-12, it is rescaled to length l. Thischanges the outward point before the alpha interpolation. Mispricing retries usethe raw outward point. Restart invalidates the automatic direction until a subsequent accepted centerprovides a new normalized subgradient. Retaining the old vector alone does notmake it valid. The 54-case parameter corpus covers this capacity-row transition.

title: Enumerated node MIP with HiGHS
heading: Enumerated node MIP with HiGHS
text: Enumerated node MIP with HiGHS Documentation index · Tree lifecycle ·BALDES options BALDES can solve a complete enumerated node master with HiGHS, while keepingClp for column generation. The integer solve uses a separate HiGHS instanceand leaves the source LP, its solution/basis, and sibling snapshots untouched.

title: Enumerated node MIP with HiGHS
heading: Controls and API

title: Enumerated node MIP with HiGHS
heading: Enumeration gate
text: Enumeration gate The route universe must be complete and its route count must not exceed theconfigured threshold. Equality and a completed empty universe are accepted.BALDESmaxNumOfEnumSolutionsForMIP defaults to 10,000;BALDESmaxNumOfEnumSolsForEndOfNodeMIP defaults to zero and is raised to at leastthe normal threshold. An incomplete universe never passes the gate. Settingonly the end-of-node option to zero does not disable the solve, because the normal threshold stillraises it. The gate counts retained enumerated routes before adding anypreviously priced elementary witness routes to the integer model.

title: Enumerated node MIP with HiGHS
heading: Preserving node semantics
text: Preserving node semantics The snapshot adapter copies the current physical row order, including baserows, inherited typed branches, and every active capacity, rank-one, strongk-path and route-load knapsack row. It rebuilds route columns using currentbase/branch coefficients and full-memory cut coefficients. It preservesexisting route upper bounds, including zero bounds. Artificial columns areomitted, so finite artificial penalties cannot masquerade as feasibility. Previously priced elementary routes are independently reconstructed andvalidated before being retained as possible witnesses. Enumeration can haveremoved a previously found incumbent route at its cutoff; retaining validatedold routes avoids losing that witness. Every added route still receives everybranch and active cut row. EnumeratedMipOutput::coverage_cutoff records the incumbent under which theuniverse was restricted (or the existing 1e12 fallback). A proof about thismatrix alone cannot exclude solutions above that cutoff. The tree uses at mostthe minimum of the proved MIP bound and that coverage cutoff. It records avalidated routing witness before closing a gap. Without a witness, a finitecoverage cutoff cannot establish global infeasibility. For snapshots with fixed partial routes,the integer model uses residual row bounds and a fixed objective offset. Returnedbounds and objectives include that offset, and route_values includes the fixedroutes when a witness is available, including a completed empty remainder.

title: Enumerated node MIP with HiGHS
heading: Outcomes
text: Outcomes Outcome Interpretation Optimal HiGHS proved the integer model optimal and supplied a validated improving witness Infeasible HiGHS proved the transferred integer model infeasible; node interpretation still depends on enumeration coverage ObjectiveCutoff The proved integer optimum does not improve the caller's cutoff; no feasible incumbent is invented from that cutoff TimeLimit / NodeLimit Unfinished solve; any validated improving incumbent is retained, but the tree does not treat the limit as a proof Incomplete Other or ambiguous statuses, including unbounded-or-infeasible and unusable witnesses; no node-closing proof A finite objective_cutoff filters improving witnesses after solving; it isnot installed as a HiGHS search cutoff. The source model is copied beforesolving, so a supplied cutoff never substitutes for a feasible incumbent.Coefficients with nonzero magnitude at most 1e-12 are rejected to avoidsilent matrix changes in HiGHS. HiGHS relative and absolute MIP gaps are set to zero. Its model status isretained in MipOutput::solver_status, with solution, dual bound, node count,simplex iterations, and elapsed time. Tree JSON adds enumerated_mip_calls andenumerated_mip_nodes; its existing mip_nodes includes this work too.

title: Enumerated node MIP with HiGHS
heading: Limitations
text: Limitations BALDES currently runs the optional solve after node evaluation. A handoffinside column generation, new cut separation during integer solving, andmultiple pricing networks remain outside this implementation. Active rowsare all retained.

title: Enumerated node MIP with HiGHS
heading: Custom CG enumeration controllers
text: Custom CG enumeration controllers The built-in routing controller transfers enumerated columns through an atomicLP copy. If enumeration, regeneration, insertion or remapping fails, it restorespricing state and continues ordinary CG. column_generation::Output::enumeration_failureretains the last transfer error; it does not itself change the solve status.Incomplete retained enumerations are discarded before pricing or inspection.Within a CG solve, a successful handoff is not repeated for an unchangedformulation. Reported row, coefficient or domain changes permit another handoff.Retained generated columns are synchronized before the transaction commits. A custom Rust Controller that implements enumerated_universe must alsoimplement begin_enumeration_transaction and finish_enumeration_transaction.The begin hook saves all mutable state used by enumeration, regeneration,column remapping and retained-pool synchronization, then returns true.The finish hook commits on true andrestores that saved state on false; restoration must be infallible. A successfulfixing pass returning no universe may commit valid partial deductions.Controllers without these hooks decline the optional transfer. Custom LPbackends must implement LpMaster::try_clone_for_transaction; Clp and HiGHSalready provide independent copies. The live LP is replaced only after everyfallible operation succeeds.

title: BALDES pricing options
heading: HGS initial columns and master backends
text:
HGS initial columns and master backends Run HGS for a separate, positive search budget before solving the root or tree: cargo run --release --features clp --bin baldes -- \
  cvrp instances/cvrplib/E-n22-k4.vrp --hgs-time 10 --hgs-columns all --tree
 --hgs-columns best (default) inserts routes from the best feasible HGS solution.all retains distinct routes seen during population insertion, including thoselater discarded or lost at a restart. A positive integer such as--hgs-columns 100 inserts up to 100 cheapest new feasible routes, ranked byoriginal arc-cost sum, with arc IDs breaking ties. Validation and deduplicationhappen before ranking; routes already supplied as initial columns do not consumethis quota.If fewer routes are available, all available routes are inserted. This rankinguses route cost, not reduced cost or whole-solution quality. Every candidateis replayed against the actual graph, using its resource bounds and arc costs;HGS's integer demands do not establish original-model feasibility. HGS uses theinstance's distance convention, with full-precision unrounded distances forSolomon instances by default. --rounding tenth explicitly enables truncatedtenths in both HGS and the target graph; --rounding none keeps unroundeddistances. Explicit distance matrices retain their supplied precision. A complete best plansupplies an incumbent only after original-model validation. --seed controlsthe random seed. HGS runs before the solver's --time budget starts; its searchlimit is cooperative, checked between HGS operations. Keeping all encounteredroutes uses more memory than keeping only the best plan. Select native IPM for restricted-master solves with --master ipm. Thisselection automatically disables dual stabilization, including at descendantnodes. The default remains --master clp. IPM solves are rebuilt from thecurrent sparse matrix and return their own primal values, duals, and reducedcosts. Clp still stores the mutable model and snapshots, so the routing drivercontinues to require the clp build feature. Basis-dependent cut retirement isskipped for IPM; it has no simplex basis. The separate conservative-boundcertificate routine retains its bounded auxiliary Clp solve. IPM time limits are cooperative,checked between Newton iterations; a factorization may exceed the remainingbudget before control returns. Numerical failures are reported as errors. During column generation, IPM uses the bound-driven accuracy rule fromMunari and Gondzio (2013), Section 3.1, Algorithm 1(Munari and Gondzio (2013), p. 2029). It starts with epsilon = 0.5, thenuses epsilon = min(1, gap / 10) with a numerical floor of 1e-9, wheregap = max(0, UB - LB) / (1 + abs(UB)). UB is the best artificial-freerestricted-master primal objective; LB comes only from exact LP pricing.Integer incumbents, heuristic pricing estimates, and stronger integer-domaincertificates do not control IPM accuracy. New cuts reset these accuracy bounds.Only the optimality gap is relaxed; primal and dual feasibility remain at1e-9. Exhausted pricing triggers an accurate master solve and another pricingcheck before separation or completion. Standalone master solves and strongbranching retain accurate solves. The requested tolerance is available asmaster_gap_tolerance in Rust's column-generation iteration history. This implements the paper's adaptive master accuracy. IPM still rebuilds eachrestricted master; the stored-interior-iterate warm starts in Section 3.4 andearly cut generation in Algorithm 2 are not implemented by this option. Select HiGHS for restricted-master LP solves with --master highs: cargo build --release --features clp,highs
./target/release/baldes vrptw instances/R101.txt --customers 25 --master highs --log
 HiGHS preserves the requested stabilization setting; use --no-stabilizationto turn it off. The native HiGHS instance persists across LP solves. Row/columninsertion, cost and coefficient edits, RHS/bound changes, and cleanup updatethat instance directly, retaining its basis and reusable simplex state. Theadapter also reuses solution buffers, batches row/column insertion, and servesan unchanged optimal LP from its cache without another native solve. Node forks copy the sparse matrix in bulk and install the source's currentnative basis into an independent HiGHS instance. A child refactorizes its ownbasis once; siblings never share mutable solver state. Solutions, reduced costs,and cut-cleanup basis statuses come from HiGHS. HiGHS owns the only nativematrix: the adapter does not retain, update, or clone a shadow Clp model.Repeated matrix reads use a lazily populated Rust CSC snapshot, fetched in bulkand invalidated by row/column insertion, coefficient edits, or deletion. Thisavoids one native range query per column during cut replay and node restoration;cost, RHS, and bound changes retain the coefficient snapshot.Selecting a different backend converts the matrix on the next edit or solve,releases the previous native model, and starts a fresh basis. Clp/IPM share Clpmatrix storage; switching between those two retains that storage.Clp still solves the separate bounded certificate auxiliary LP. Selecting HiGHSwithout the highs build featurereturns an explicit error. Enable HiGHS in make config when building with Make. Python accepts master_solver="highs"; build its extension with the highsfeature (for example, maturin develop --release --features highs).pybaldes.has_highs reports whether that build feature is available. In Rust, set RootOptions::master_solver to MasterSolver::Highs orMasterSolver::Ipm. For HGS seeding,call instance.seed_hgs(&problem, rounding, &mut options, &HgsWarmStart { ... })before passing those options to root::solve or TreeOptions::root. The typesHgsWarmStart and HgsColumns::{Best, All, Top(n)} are exported by baldes::inputs.The returned summary reports inserted/rejected columns and any validatedincumbent. Existing initial columns are retained and duplicates are skipped. Python exposes the same root options: result = pybaldes.solve_root(
    "instances/cvrplib/E-n22-k4.vrp", problem_type="cvrp",
    hgs_time=10.0, hgs_columns=100, hgs_seed=7, master_solver="ipm",
)

text:
Terminal progress Routing solves are quiet by default. --verbose, -v, or --log enables analigned column-generation table on stderr. It prints iteration 1, every tenthiteration, and the final state, followed by the CG status and work totals.--log-interval N enables the same log with a positive custom interval.Cut-count columns appear only for enabled families: Rank1, Capacity,2Path, KPath, Knapsack, and Fenchel. Each shows the number of thatfamily's rows currently in the master, including inherited cuts and excludingremoved rows. Enabled families show zero before any cuts are installed.The interval applies to each CG solve, including descendant nodes and treetrials. Each node reports its depth, master algorithm, and stabilization mode. ./target/release/baldes vrptw instances/R101.txt --customers 25 \
  --hgs-time 2 --hgs-columns 100 --master ipm --verbose
 RMP obj is the restricted-master objective and may include artificial columns;it is not a feasible routing objective or a global lower bound. Lower boundis the separately certified bound. Incumbent is the current objective upperbound; a caller-supplied root upper bound still carries its feasibilityassumption. Gap % is 100 * max(0, incumbent - bound) / max(1, abs(incumbent)).Unknown or nonfinite values appear as --. Min RC is the latest pricingminimum, +Cols counts inserted columns in that iteration, Cols is the currentmaster size including artificials, and Phase is the pricing phase. Time iselapsed wall time within the current CG call. A CG Optimal status does notby itself certify an integer routing optimum. The logger adds no color escapes or cursor control, so redirected logs remainreadable. stdout summaries and --json files retain their result formats.Standalone hgs --verbose uses the same HGS progress table; during warm starts,that table and its summary appear before the column-generation log. Rust callers set options.cg.log_interval = Some(10) (or the generic CGOptions::log_interval). Python callers use verbose=True, log_interval=10.Python's interval defaults to 10 and must be positive; verbose=False keepsCG silent.

title: Scalar resources
heading: Resource semantics
text: Resource semantics Every active coordinate participates in extension, dominance, forward/backwardjoins, route reconstruction, enumeration, branching, resource knapsack charges,conservative path domains, and exact incumbent checks. A disposable resource accumulates nonnegative arc consumption and may wait toreach a lower bound. An equality resource accumulates signed consumption withoutwaiting. Arc windows constrain the head state after extension. Initial valuesdefault to source lower bounds. Backward equality search requires fixed sinkwindows; price selects forward search when those are not fixed. Bucket indexing uses at most two selected axes, independently of scalar capacity.A resource above index one can be the main axis through Graph::main_resource.Positive EngineControls::steps or Solver::bucket_steps select additionaldisposable axes; at most one joins the main axis. Unselected resources stillparticipate in feasibility and dominance. More active resources can retain morenondominated labels and increase time and memory. Existing resource-kind,NG, budget, and certificate-eligibility restrictions still apply.

title: SIMD dispatch
heading: SIMD dispatch
text: SIMD dispatch Documentation index The optional simd feature enables four-label AVX2 dominance scans.simd-avx512 includes it and enables eight-label AVX-512F scans on Rust 1.89+.Both features are off by default. Runtime detection keeps binaries portable:AVX-512F (when compiled in), AVX2, then the portable implementation. Scansshorter than 16 remaining labels use the portable implementation. The AVX-512F kernel uses ordered comparisons, retains the exact EPSILONaddition/subtraction order, and returns the first matching label or prefixkey stop in storage order. It widens eight packed u16 NG masks into eightu64 lanes without requiring AVX-512BW, VL, DQ or VPOPCNTDQ. All loadedcolumns are checked before pointer loads; tails use the scalar kernel.The comparison tests exercise direct AVX2/AVX-512 paths and runtime dispatchagainst an independent scalar reference, including NaNs, infinities,subnormals, signed zero, epsilon boundaries, offsets and incomplete blocks.
