title: Multiple time windows
heading: Python and network JSON
text:
Python and network JSON Build Python with maturin develop --features multi-time-windows (or add thatfeature to the existing wheel build). The stateful solver exposes: solver.set_vertex_time_windows(1, 0, [(8.0, 12.0), (16.0, 20.0)])
 Network JSON, built with clp,multi-time-windows, accepts time_windows on aresource: one entry per vertex, each either null (ordinary bounds) or a nonemptylist of [lower, upper] pairs. For a three-vertex network: {
  "kind": "disposable",
  "time_windows": [null, [[8, 12], [16, 20]], null],
  "bounds": [[0, 30], [0, 18], [0, 30]]
}
 When both fields are supplied, bounds intersects the union; the second intervalin this example is effectively [16, 18]. Without the build feature the JSON fieldis rejected as unknown, rather than silently ignored. Solomon and CVRPLIB fileformats retain their existing input semantics; use the graph API or network JSONfor disjoint windows.

title: Multiple time windows
heading: Implementation and validation
text:
Implementation and validation Forward transitions choose the first admissible value at or after arrival;backward transitions search from the last interval and clip at the head beforesubtracting consumption and projecting onto the tail domain. Both intersectvertex and arc restrictions. These transitions are shared by pricing, replay,canonical path collection and elementary enumeration. Exact incumbent validationalso applies union membership using its exact arithmetic. Bucket propagation projects across gaps, and component/reachability constructionincludes the image of a whole bucket cell. A discontinuous waiting jump can thusreach a later interval without being pruned by an adjacency built for the hull.If a far cell endpoint is infeasible, the image uses a conservative hull bound.Backward bucket arcs retain both phase flags, since a gap can cross thehalfway boundary inside one input cell. Actual label resources select the phase.This can create extra dependencies and increase preparation work; no performanceimprovement is claimed. Consumption-symmetric prefix reuse is disabled on graphswith configured unions, because hull symmetry alone does not justify timereversal. Ordinary forward/backward labeling remains available. Tests compare bucket pricing with independent exhaustive integer path scheduleson randomized DAGs and elementary cyclic graphs. Regressions cover earliest andlatest projection, gap rejection, arc intersections, terminal domains, effectivesink bounds, zero-width windows, nonindexed resource coordinates, normalization,topology invalidation, halfway continuation, enumeration, JSON loading, and exactincumbent witnesses. Validation commands: cargo test -p baldes --features clp,multi-time-windows,simd --lib --test multi_time_windows --test main_pricing --test fixing_enumeration --test accumulated_resource --test porting_regressions
cargo test -p baldes --lib --test main_pricing --test fixing_enumeration --test accumulated_resource --test porting_regressions
cargo clippy -p baldes --lib --test multi_time_windows --features clp,multi-time-windows,simd
 The Python regression in python/tests/test_multi_time_windows.py passes againstthe feature-enabled extension and skips on wheels without it. Test builds usedCARGO_PROFILE_DEV_OPT_LEVEL=0, CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG=0, andCARGO_INCREMENTAL=0. Modified Rust files pass rustfmt. The broader Clippy runincluding all unit tests hits existing denied approx_constant andabsurd_extreme_comparisons lints in unrelated tests; targeted Clippy completeswith repository warnings.

title: Multi-pricing: one master, multiple pricing subproblems
heading: Multi-pricing: one master, multiple pricing subproblems
text: Multi-pricing: one master, multiple pricing subproblems Documentation index With clp, master::multi_pricing::solve solves a shared root and returns an ownednode snapshot that can be resumed or forked. Its pricing graphs share masterrows. Each Network owns a graph, a unique nonnegative ID andnonnegative multiplicity bounds. Rust models may use a finite lower bound andpositive-infinite upper bound. Local arc IDs may overlap acrossnetworks: route identities include the network ID and resource schedule. The coordinator is called multi-pricing because one master coordinatesmultiple pricing subproblems. A network is an individual subproblem's graphand route family. Subproblems may share a vehicle type or represent differenttypes, depots or resources; heterogeneity is optional. This is independent ofusing several CPU cores for a single pricing problem. Problem.rows defines the shared constraints. Network.arc_entries containsone list of (shared_row, coefficient) pairs per physical arc, in graph order.route_entries adds coefficients charged once per route. The coordinator addsthe network multiplicity rows separately; callers do not include them in theshared-row indices. Arc costs define original route costs. Variable-costmapping used internally by pricing does not modify the supplied graphs.Physical multiplicity rows appear in input-network order: a finite upper rowcomes first, then a lower row when the lower bound is positive. An infiniteupper bound adds no row. Shared rows follow these multiplicity rows in theiroriginal order. In Rust, use Window { lower: 0., upper: f64::INFINITY } for an unlimited routecount; Window::new remains the finite scalar-resource window constructor.Original shared rows can prove a finite remaining count, which tightens futurecolumns and bound compensation and survives forks/fixing. If a negative reducedcost has no finite count bound, the estimate remains unknown while pricing cancontinue. A zero reduced cost does not multiply infinity. Truly unboundednegative-cost route directions report an unbounded backend solve. JSON uses"multiplicity": [0, null] for an unlimited upper count. The lower count mustremain finite and nonnegative. The coordinator maintains independent pricing state, combines columns into onerestricted master and aggregates each network's multiplicity contribution andstabilization subgradient. Output.oracle_calls counts individual oracle calls;Output.master.pricing_calls counts batches. Output.values gives the currentrestricted-master quantity for every route in Output.routes. Phase estimates guide stabilization. Published lower bounds additionally usegraph-walk relaxations with downward arithmetic. If a negative cycle preventsa resource-free bound, nonnegative scalar consumption and bounded resourcewindows can justify a finite walk-length limit. The proof can combine dimensionswith different units: it sums their individual positive-arc occurrence limits.Arcs consuming zero on every selected dimension must form an acyclic graph.Thus different cycles may consume different resources. The fallback uses a bounded workbudget. Without a justified limit, or after arithmetic failure, budget exhaustionor an unavailable required path, the certificate remains unknown. A finiteresource-aware bound can still be too weak to close the gap. In certified mode, unavailable certificates cannot closethe gap; numerical mode retains its separate exact-pricing estimate. Finiteartificial penaltiesalso do not certify original-model infeasibility. A stalled restricted LP canstill contain artificial variables; its objective and route quantities arenot then an original feasible solution.

title: Multi-pricing: one master, multiple pricing subproblems
heading: Assignment tree
text: Assignment tree solve_assignment_tree(problem, AssignmentTreeOptions) runs a best-bound treeusing network-aware snapshots. It tries assignment rows, declared integer mastervariables, total network multiplicities, then original physical-arc activities. It returns network-taggedinteger route quantities, an incumbent, selected bound mode, frontier bound andnode/work-limit status. Integer witnesses replay original graph resources,shared rows and original multiplicities with exact sums; objectives round upward.Fixed routes are included in this replay. A rounded labeling resource profilealone never authorizes an incumbent or fixed route. Rust callers can run snapshot.solve_assignment_tree(options) after installingshared nonlinear rows, fixing routes or restricting master variables. It forksthe snapshot and retains cuts, bounds, fixed contributions and complete routeuniverses. A zero-node run preserves only the inherited bound of the requestedbound mode; a numerical bound is not promoted to a certificate. Every fallback split is an integer-valid floor/ceiling disjunction on anoriginal quantity. Continuous master variables are never branched as integers.These families still do not cover every fractional route decomposition; such anode remains Incomplete. An exact whole-original-flow contradiction can closea node. Positive artificials, a stalled LP or incomplete certification alone donot prove infeasibility. Complete-master integer deductions retain the explicitinteger-domain policy.Node/time limits retain the open-frontier bound. Bounds on fixed-route nodesare newly certified only when their RHS, offset and residual multiplicityreductions are exact; otherwise valid inherited certificates remain available,but a new original-domain bound stays unknown.

text: Finite column imports Rust callers can combine routing networks with explicitly declared finiteoriginal-vector column domains using multi_pricing::imported::solve. Seefinite column imports for coordinate links, column fixing,multiplicity bounds, identity mapping and complete-domain MIP.

title: Multi-pricing: one master, multiple pricing subproblems
heading: Independent master variables
text: Independent master variables solve_with_master_variables(problem, variables, options) adds independentMasterVariable definitions to the shared master. Each definition has its ownID, objective cost, signed bounds (finite, one-sided or free), integrality flag and shared-rowcoefficients. IDs are independent of network and arc IDs. Root LPs relaxintegrality; complete-domain MIP retains it. Output.master_values returnsoriginal values by ID, separately from network-tagged routes. For a model with no pricing subproblems, Rust callers can usesolve_master(rows, variables, options). It solves the continuous relaxation andreturns the same snapshot API. Signed, one-sided, free and integer variablesretain their usual contracts. The empty pricing family is complete immediately:snapshot.solve_enumerated_mip(options) needs no preceding enumeration, andsnapshot.solve_assignment_tree(options) branches integer master variables.No dummy network is required. A Problem::<D> with an empty networks list isalso accepted by solve_with_master_variables, for any compile-time D.An empty model has objective zero; original-row contradictions are available tothe tree as preprocessing proofs. This Rust API does not add master-variablefields to the CLI/Python JSON schema. Snapshots support with_master_variable_bounds(id, bounds) for restrictions orfixing. with_master_row(row, network_coefficients, master_coefficients) couplesthese variables to additive network activities;with_rank_one_master_row(row, floor_coefficients, master_coefficients) couplesthem to nonlinear floor rows. Existing parent restrictions remain in force.All operations preserve independent sibling snapshots. The corresponding treeentry point is solve_assignment_tree_with_master_variables. Signed variables retain their original coefficients and costs. Their boundsparticipate in joint propagation, and bounds tightened by original constraintsreach static master columns and publication certificates. Inferred positivelower bounds and negative upper bounds are also published as original-variablerows, so the LP, warm snapshots and MIP enforce those bounds. A bounded exactrow-reduction pass also combines shared constraints with linear equalities thatlink master variables. For example, a + b >= 1.5 and m = a + b implym >= 1.5; the optional integer policy strengthens this to m >= 2 when mis integer. The pass retains support-reducing sums/differences only, rejectsrounded coefficients/RHS values, and reserves most work for ordinary propagation.It does not treat nonlinear row envelopes as equalities. Continuous mastervalues remain continuous when route quantities are made integer in MIP andwitness validation. Infinite endpoints represent mathematical domains. An adverse dual point on anunbounded component can leave the published bound unknown. Original shared rowsmay supply a finite proof-only bound even with preprocessing disabled; this doesnot change the snapshot or replace infinity with a finite modeling cap.

title: Multi-pricing: one master, multiple pricing subproblems
heading: Original activities, multiplicities and nonlinear rows
text: Original activities, multiplicities and nonlinear rows Rust snapshots expose with_activity_bounds(bounds, coefficients) to restrictan aggregate original variable across networks. Each RowCoefficients suppliesarc coefficients and a once-per-route coefficient for its network. Equal lowerand upper bounds fix the activity. with_multiplicity(network, bounds) boundsthe total route count, including fixed copies. Both operations fork the nodeand preserve restrictions in future pricing, descendants and enumeration. Activity bounds constrain the aggregate master activity. For example, an upperbound of 0.25 remains a fractional activity cap in the continuous relaxation.It is not an arc-availability flag. Opting into integer-domain preprocessing canstrengthen a proved integer activity cap below one to zero. Pricing supportsare defined separately by the graph and registered restrictions. with_rank_one_row(row, coefficients) installs a shared nonlinear row. EachRankOneCoefficients defines a network's coefficient asfloor(sum of visited vertex weights / denominator). Weights count each visit,lie between zero and denominator minus one, and must be zero at both terminals.Supported denominators are 1–7. The caller supplies a valid row. Fixed routes subtract their nonlinearcoefficient from its RHS, including when the row is installed after fixing.Pricing uses full memory; master coefficients retain the actual physical arcs.with_registered_cut_row(row, coefficients) accepts RegisteredCutCoefficientsfor existing packing, covering, limited-memory, arc-weighted and strong k-pathdescriptors. with_registered_cut_master_row also couples independent mastervariables. Use physical vertex/arc IDs for the selected network and consistentgraph-specific supports. Weights must be nonnegative and below the denominator(1–7); unsupported original-set mappings and incompatible descriptors arerejected. The caller supplies a valid inequality; these methods do not separatecuts automatically. Fixed-route shifts and future-column coefficients use theregistered memory contract. with_composite_cut_row(row, coefficients) sums several registered descriptorsinto one shared row, including multiple terms from the same network.with_composite_cut_master_row couples this sum to independent master variables.Repeated descriptors contribute repeatedly. Pricing applies the shared row dualto every term; replay and fixed-route shifts use their summed coefficient.This API expresses a sum, not an indicator that any term is present. The originalwith_registered_cut_row still rejects duplicate network descriptors. These Rust methods are not currently exposed in the JSON or Python model schema. with_presence_row(row, coefficients) installs a caller-supplied valid nonlinearrow over original-variable events. Each PresenceCoefficients supplies anetwork ID, a PresenceRow and event lists aligned with physical graph arcs.Mode::PairCount counts satisfied stored pairs, including duplicates;Mode::AnyPair contributes at most one. Repeated emission of an event does notmultiply its contribution. with_presence_master_row also couples independentmaster variables. All row senses are supported. Fixing replays the actualcoefficient, including rows appended after the fix; pricing, snapshots andcomplete enumeration/MIP use the same event definition. Original-domain certificates keep active presence rows together in a boundedwalk-state search. It charges actual event-pair increments using directedarithmetic, including duplicate pairs, repeated events and either dual sign.Event IDs are local to each row. Sparse event compression avoids allocating bythe largest event ID. Resource-derived walk-length bounds can cover adversecycles; otherwise an adverse cycle leaves this improvement unknown. Work ortime exhaustion falls back to the existing conservative relaxation. Thesecertificates do not require complete enumeration. Original-domain preprocessing drops nonnegative presence terms from <=relaxations and bounds them by the maximum coefficient times multiplicity for>= relaxations. When static terms exhaust the upper side of a <= or equalityrow, preprocessing searches source-to-sink walks with zero presence coefficient.It considers all pairs in that descriptor jointly, including events spread overseveral arcs, and forbids physical arcs absent from every such walk. The searchignores resources and elementarity, so its walk domain contains every feasibleroute. Cycles and repeated events are supported; equivalent incidence statesat the same vertex are merged. Sparse event IDs do not allocate the entiredeclared event domain. All searches share the preprocessing work budget. Anunfinished search publishes no additional walk-support exclusions; previouslyproved exclusions remain valid. These deductions participate in the jointflow/static-variable fixed point across pricing subproblems. Certified bounds can belooser than the numerical LP because their original-domain relaxation dropspositive presence penalties when joint presence-state certification exhausts itswork/time allowance; such a run can remain Stalled until a strongerproof or complete enumeration closes the gap. Registered cut rows also support original-domain zero-coefficient propagation.When directed bounds prove that static contributions exhaust a nonnegativerow's <= budget, every registered kernel in that row must be zero. A boundedwalk search keeps the kernels' packing remainders jointly, including vertex orphysical-arc memory resets. Covering and strong-entry kernels reject supporthits; repeated composite descriptors keep their sum semantics. Arcs absentfrom all zero-coefficient source-to-sink walks are forbidden before enumeration.The search ignores route resources and elementarity, so its walk domain is asafe superset. Interrupted searches publish no partial walk exclusions. These deductions share the flow/resource/presence work budget and repeat to ajoint fixed point. Signed static compensation or a positive fractional rowbudget prevents unjustified zero deductions. This is a necessary zero-budgetrule, not a general nonlinear optimizer or automatic cut separator. with_resource_knapsack_row(row, coefficients) installs a shared <= rowusing ResourceKnapsackCoefficients (network, resource coordinate, graph scaleand monotone nonnegative step cut). with_resource_knapsack_master_row alsocouples independent master variables. This API supports nonnegativeconsumption, initial usage and vertex/arc windows on a common power-of-two grid.The grid spacing must lie between 2^-18 and 1, and each value must use atmost 2^52 grid units. Integer schedules retain their existing range; fractionssuch as 0.5 and 0.125 are supported when the complete schedule fits thisrange. Finer binary fractions, negative values, and schedules requiring moregrid units are rejected before installation.Disposable resources may wait; equality resources must meet their windowswithout waiting. Coefficients use the earliest forward scalar schedule replayedfrom physical arcs; cached route profiles cannot change them. Pricing uses graphscaling and unrounded nonpositive duals. Fractional schedules, nonzero initial usage, waiting windows, intermediatecapacity changes and equality resources select forward-only pricing for theaffected network. Thispreserves the coefficient contract even if a caller requests bidirectionalsearch. Zero-initial integer disposable loads with uniform capacity retain theexisting bidirectional option. Fixed routes shift these rows, and descendants, enumeration and mixed MIPretain them. Complete-domain preprocessing can fix route quantities from thestep coefficients. Before enumeration, a row that permits only zero resourcepenalty can also forbid original arcs whose consumption guarantees a positivestep coefficient. Directed bounds on static variables must first prove that nonegative static contribution can compensate those penalties. Flow conservationthen propagates the arc fixings. The original-domain flow and resource-zerorules repeat while deductions enable each other, sharing one work budget.preprocessing_report().propagation.work_used reports the logical work spent.Incomplete budgeted passes retain valid partial deductions without claiming afixed point. Before complete enumeration, the original-domain certificatemay drop their nonnegative pricing penalty for a weaker valid lower bound;this need not close the LP gap. These methods require caller-supplied validinequalities and do not automatically separate resource-knapsack cuts. Node solves automatically propagate a joint arc-flow relaxation across networks.It includes shared activities, flow conservation and route multiplicities;nonlinear rows contribute safe activity envelopes. Proved-zero arc usage forbidsthat arc in future pricing and fixes affected retained columns to zero. Aftercomplete enumeration, a second pass can also deduce zero route quantities fromnonlinear coefficients. Missing future columns never justify these deductions. Use options.preprocessing.enabled = false to disable propagation, or adjustoptions.preprocessing.work_limit. snapshot.preprocess() runs the defaultpolicy on a fork; preprocess_with_options() supplies a separate budget.preprocessing_report() exposes aggregate arc and multiplicity bounds, workcompletion, route caps, zero fixings, and reasons for skipping unsafe arithmetic.Positive aggregate arc bounds are not per-route resource windows. After completetransfer, proved positive route-quantity caps are installed in the master andpreserved through cleanup, regeneration and descendants. Fixing copies of a routereduces its remaining cap. Upper-active columns may have negative reduced costs;the numerical and certified bounds account for these caps. Inexact coefficientaggregation or fixed-route reductions skip deductions. Exhausted work preservesvalid partial deductions. The default policy preserves the continuous LP and reports preprocessinginfeasibility without independently pruning a tree node. Setoptions.preprocessing.integer_domains = true to use original integer route,arc-usage and multiplicity domains, together with each master variable's declaredintegrality. Continuous master variables remain continuous. With this explicitpolicy, a proved contradiction can close an integer tree node even when its LPrelaxation is feasible. Reports distinguish inferred master-variable boundsfrom network activity bounds. Disabling propagation later does not widen asnapshot that already contains deductions; reuse an earlier ancestor for itsoriginal continuous relaxation.

title: Multi-pricing: one master, multiple pricing subproblems
heading: Limitations
text: Limitations The supported lifecycle supports additive rows and explicit full-memory floorrows through Rust. Automatic nonlinear cut separation,reduced-cost-pruned enumeration with proved coverage,other branching families and broader resource-awarecertificates remain open. Rust and Python expose the supportedshared-master node lifecycle. The existing single-network routing entrypoints retain their current behavior.

title: Multi-pricing: one master, multiple pricing subproblems
heading: CLI
text:
CLI The multi-pricing command accepts an explicit JSON model, rather than a Solomoninstance. It uses Clp and supports both shared roots and the assignment tree: cargo build --offline --features clp --bin baldes
target/debug/baldes multi-pricing examples/networks/triangle.json --json root.json
target/debug/baldes multi-pricing examples/networks/triangle.json --tree --json tree.json
# JSON alone on stdout, suitable for a pipe:
target/debug/baldes multi-pricing examples/networks/triangle.json --tree --json -
 The example has shared LP optimum 1.5 and integer optimum 2. --time,--iterations, --nodes, --bound-mode, --no-stabilization,--artificial-cost, --option NAME=VALUE, and --log-interval control solves.Run baldes multi-pricing --help for details. The previous networks command remains an alias. Unsupported routing flags are errors.A successful command means the run completed and produced a result: inspectstatus and open_nodes for NodeLimit, TimeLimit or Incomplete outcomes. A model contains rows and networks. Rows use sense: "eq" | "le" | "ge"and a finite rhs. Each network has a unique nonnegative id, a verticescount, [lower, upper] fleet multiplicity, and an arcs list. Optionalfields are source (default zero), sink (default last vertex), resources,route_entries and ng. Vertex indices and shared-row indices are zero based.Arc IDs are assigned consecutively in each network's input order, starting atzero; overlapping IDs in different networks are supported. Each arc provides tail, head, cost and optional entries pairs[shared_row, coefficient]. Its optional consumption and bounds arraysmust match the resource count when nonempty. Arc bounds contain either[lower, upper] or null for each resource. Missing consumption is zero.Each resource has kind: "disposable" (default) or "equality", an optionalinitial value, and optional bounds with one [lower, upper] pair per vertex.Default resource bounds are [0, 100000]. Network route_entries are chargedonce per route. Optional ng contains one neighborhood list per vertex.Resources may be empty; the maximum count is the build's scalar capacity.Unknown fields, nonfinite values and inconsistent dimensions are rejected. Result routes retain network, local arcs, nodes, cost, resource states andvalue. A root's route_index identifies its registry entry for later fixing;zero-valued registered routes are retained too. fixed_routes lists fixedquantities separately. Unknown/nonfinite bounds and absent objectives are JSONnull, not Infinity. Root mode reports an LP relaxation; tree mode reportsan independently replayed integer witness when available. Their mode andbound_mode fields preserve that distinction.

title: Multi-pricing: one master, multiple pricing subproblems
heading: Python
text:
Python Install the extension with Clp support (the Python build's default). The typedinputs use the same JSON schema as the CLI, allowing a single model to driveboth interfaces: from pybaldes import NetworkProblem, solve_networks

problem = NetworkProblem.from_file("examples/networks/triangle.json")
root = solve_networks(problem)
assert root.lp == 1.5
integer = problem.solve(tree=True)
assert integer.incumbent == 2.0

candidate = root.snapshot.fractional_assignments()[0]
left = root.snapshot.branch_assignment(
    candidate.shared_row, candidate.network, True,
)
right = root.snapshot.branch_assignment(
    candidate.shared_row, candidate.network, False,
)
assert left.solve().lp == 2.0
assert right.solve().lp == 2.0
assert root.snapshot.solve().lp == 1.5
 Models can also be constructed with NetworkProblem, SharedRow,PricingNetwork, PricingArc and PricingResource dataclasses. Useproblem.to_json() to export them for the CLI. NetworkResult.to_json()serializes owned result data and excludes its native snapshot. Root snapshots additionally expose with_row(SharedRow(...), coefficients)with NetworkRowCoefficients(network, arcs, per_route=0), andfix_route(route_index, quantity=1). Child operations return independentNetworkNode objects; node.solve(**options) returns a new result and snapshot.Quantities fixed in Python must be positive integers. Node handles belong toone Python thread and root/node calls keep the GIL. Fresh tree=True callsrelease the GIL and return owned results without a resumable snapshot. The root/tree solve accepts time_limit, max_iterations, node_limit,stabilize, bound_mode, artificial_cost, log_interval andpricing_options. Resuming a snapshot accepts node options; tree=Truerequires a fresh model. Tree iteration, pricing-batch and individual oraclecounts aggregate the evaluated nodes; nodes and open_nodes report tree work.

title: Multi-pricing: one master, multiple pricing subproblems
heading: Complete enumeration and integer transfer
text:
Complete enumeration and integer transfer Enumeration is opt-in. Options.enumeration in Rust, enumerate=True inPython, or --enumerate in the CLI attempts a bounded full-domain transferat an accurate exact pricing checkpoint with no improving columns or positiveartificials. This can strengthen an NG master toits elementary-route master. Every enabled network must complete before anycolumns are committed. Existing valid columns and their bounds remain; cycliccolumns outside the integer domain are fixed to zero. All current physicalrows, including additive cuts/branches, remain in place. Descendants reuse thecomplete route universe and evaluate new row coefficients on it. Transfer supports nonempty physically elementary paths with disposable andscalar equality resources. Equality paths are collected through a disposablesuperset, then checked against the original equality transitions; paths feasibleonly by waiting are excluded. Equality resources with a non-fixed sinkwindow use forward pricing even if another direction was requested; backwardpricing requires a fixed terminal resource value. Graphs containing direct source/sink routesdecline transfer because empty-route integer semantics are not yet defined. Collection uses a downward resource relaxationthat cannot discard an exact-feasible path, then independently replays originalresources. Negative-consumption equality domains remain unavailable throughthis collector. Unsupported resources, ambiguous canonical replay, global work/path/storage limits or timeout leave the transfer unavailable. Normal pricing remainsusable. Limits apply across all enabled networks, not independently per network.The default candidate limit is 10,000, work limit 10,000,000, stored-arc limit1,000,000 and attempt budget one second. Disabled networks contribute no routes. enumeration_reports distinguishes no attempt, complete transfer and failure.Each report records attempts, per-network counts, route count, newly transferredcolumns and the failure reason. A repeated transfer on a complete snapshot doesnot duplicate columns. Failed transfers do not retain a partial universe.Each solve attempts at most one adaptive transfer, then resumes CG within theoriginal time and iteration limits. Backend transfer failures retain the originalmaster and warm start. A later solve can retry with different enumeration limits.The explicit Rust snapshot.enumerate(...) method attempts transfer immediately. No reduced-cost/objective cutoff removes paths during this collection; coverageis the full supported domain, including incumbent routes. Rust callers can separately request snapshot.enumerate_below(cutoff, &limits)to collect routes needed by integer solutions strictly below a finite objectivecutoff. This returns an immutable CutoffEnumeration, with coverage_cutoff(),report(), routes(), dual_point() and cost_bounds(). Limits cover allnetworks and proof preparation. Missing original-domain bounds, unsupportedresource replay and exhausted budgets return an error; the source snapshotremains usable. This API currently requires a snapshot that has not alreadyinstalled a full enumerated universe. With highs, call view.solve_mip(&MipOptions::default()) on that view. ItsObjectiveCutoff outcome means no integer solution improves the effectivecutoff; it does not mean the original model is infeasible. Time/node limits remain explicit. A cutoff supplied by the callerdoes not itself establish a feasible incumbent. The view cannot be resumed asan original-domain LP or attached to a different snapshot. Its rows, fixedcontributions and caps are frozen; derive a new view from each changed node.The adaptive CG handoff above continues to use full-domain enumeration.When tree enumerated_mip is enabled and full transfer is unavailable, the treetries cutoff enumeration using its validated incumbent or the smaller suppliedMIP cutoff. A failed attempt leaves normal branching available. Numerical modecan close a node from a sufficient MIP bound; certified mode uses returnedwitnesses without promoting a numerical MIP bound to a certificate. The CLI accepts --mip-cutoff X with --tree --enumerated-mip. The matchingJSON solve option is mip_objective_cutoff (finite number, or null for no suppliedcutoff). Reports include coverage_cutoff: null denotes full-domain coverage;a number denotes coverage only below that objective. A cutoff without anincumbent cannot close the original tree merely because its restricted poolhas no improving integer solution.Python's solve_networks(..., tree=True, enumerated_mip=True, mip_objective_cutoff=...) uses the same policy. EachNetworkEnumerationReport.coverage_cutoff identifies the scope of its pool;None means full-domain coverage. With the optional highs feature, the tree can solve a complete transferredcopy as an integer model. Artificial columns are fixed to zero, and routebounds, fleet rows, shared rows, inherited cuts/branches, fixed-route RHScontributions and objective offsets are retained. If LP cleanup retired a route,the private MIP model restores it from the complete universe and reapplies itscap before solving. The original snapshot remains unchanged. Positive integer routes arereplayed against the original graph and original rows before an incumbent ispublished. Source masters and siblings remain unchanged after any MIP outcome. cargo build --offline --features clp,highs --bin baldes
target/debug/baldes multi-pricing examples/networks/triangle.json --tree --enumerated-mip --json -
# Force enumeration to decline and normal pricing/branching to continue:
target/debug/baldes multi-pricing examples/networks/triangle.json --tree --enumerated-mip --enumeration-route-limit 5 --json -
 --enumerated-mip requires --tree and HiGHS support; it also enables enumeration.--enumeration-time, --mip-time and --mip-nodes control per-attempt budgets.MIP timeout/node limits/backend failure do not authorize pricing termination.enumerated_mip_calls, enumerated_mip_nodes and enumerated_mip_failures reportwork and fallback. Full-MIP numerical proof outcomes may close numerical-modenodes; they never become certified-mode lower-bound certificates. A cutoffwithout a validated witness is not an incumbent or an infeasibility claim. Python uses the same options and reports: from pybaldes import NetworkProblem
problem = NetworkProblem.from_file("examples/networks/triangle.json")
root = problem.solve(enumerate=True)
assert root.enumeration_reports[0].complete
integer = root.snapshot.solve_enumerated_mip(time_limit=1.0)
assert integer.status == "Optimal" and integer.incumbent == 2.0
# Or combine node enumeration and MIP with the tree:
tree = problem.solve(tree=True, enumerated_mip=True)
assert tree.nodes == 1 and tree.incumbent == 2.0
 node.solve(enumerate=True, enumeration_route_limit=..., enumeration_work_limit=..., enumeration_stored_arc_limit=..., enumeration_time_limit=...) prepares a resumednode and returns a new snapshot. solve_enumerated_mip returns None when thenode has not completed transfer. Its optional objective_cutoff filters improvingwitnesses without restricting enumeration; ObjectiveCutoff remains distinctfrom Infeasible. MIP calls on existing Python snapshots keep the GIL and theirthread ownership. Fresh tree calls retain the existing GIL-release behavior. For Python, build with maturin develop --features highs (Clp is enabled bydefault). Clp-only builds still support complete enumeration; they reject MIPrequests explicitly.

title: Multi-pricing: one master, multiple pricing subproblems
heading: Grouped accumulated-resource branches
text:
Grouped accumulated-resource branches A group can span several pricing networks. Name its original shared packing row,one resource coordinate, a stored threshold, and the physical arc IDs belongingto the group in each network. The packing row must prove at most one occurrence:its sense is eq or le, its RHS is at most one, all original contributions arenonnegative, and each member arc has a coefficient of at least one. Signedmaster-variable domains must also preserve nonnegative packing contributions. use baldes::master::multi_pricing::ResourceGroupMember;
let members = vec![
    ResourceGroupMember { network: 7, arcs: vec![0, 2] },
    ResourceGroupMember { network: 42, arcs: vec![0, 2] },
];
let lower = parent.with_resource_group_branch(0, 0, 1.5, false, &members)?;
let upper = parent.with_resource_group_branch(0, 0, 1.5, true, &members)?;
 Both children include the boundary threshold - 1e-6. The lower child requiresresource usage at most that boundary; the upper child requires usage at leastit. Disposable resources can wait to satisfy an upper window. Equality resourcescannot wait. Restrictions cover every occurrence of each listed physical arc,including parallel alternatives. Other networks and arcs remain available. Shared trees also generate disposable-resource groups automatically from originalunit packing rows. They combine physical occurrences across networks, account forancestor windows and use feasible forward/backward schedule intervals to selecta threshold. Rust callers can inspect the current solved node withparent.resource_group_candidates(1e-6)? and attach either side withcandidate.apply(&parent, upper)?. The tree tries these candidates before itsassignment and aggregate-activity fallbacks. A failed attachment leaves theparent reusable and causes the tree to try another disjunction. Children own their restrictions through solves, further branches, route fixing,enumeration and MIP. Parent and sibling snapshots remain reusable. Retainedschedules refresh under their existing route tags and caps. Fixed schedulesremain fixed; a contradictory child is infeasible. If exact feasibility can beproved but a scalar schedule cannot be reconstructed, attachment returns anerror and preserves the parent. Resource-load rows on a disposable coordinate that an upper branch can re-timerequire complete enumeration before attachment. This keeps the rows' originalpath-load semantics. Call parent.enumerate(&limits) first; the same conditionapplies when adding such a row after a branch. Rows on other coordinates andpath-based additive or registered rows keep their usual workflow. Python exposes the same owned operation: from pybaldes import NetworkResourceGroupMember
members = (NetworkResourceGroupMember(7, (0, 2)),
           NetworkResourceGroupMember(42, (0, 2)))
child = parent.with_resource_group_branch(0, 0, 1.5, True, members)
result = child.solve(stabilize=False)
tree = child.solve(tree=True, stabilize=False)
 For the CLI, pass a JSON array of these restrictions with--resource-branches FILE. Each object has packing_row, resource,threshold, upper and members; each member has network and arcs.The model is restricted before the requested root or tree solve. cargo run --release --features clp --bin baldes -- multi-pricing \
  examples/networks/resource_groups.json \
  --resource-branches examples/networks/resource_group_upper.json \
  --tree --bound-mode certified --json -

title: Finite column imports
heading: Finite column imports
text: Finite column imports Documentation index With clp, Rust callers can import finite column domains throughmaster::multi_pricing::imported. Routing networks are optional. Importedcolumns are original-vector patterns, so this interface also supports finitenon-routing models without constructing synthetic routes.

title: Finite column imports
heading: Model contract
text: Model contract Supply the ordinary shared Problem<D>, original MasterVariable definitionsand a list of imported::Subproblem definitions. Each subproblem declares: A nonnegative ID, distinct from other imported subproblems and routing IDs. The original variable IDs in its coordinate support. Nonnegative total multiplicity bounds, with an optional infinite upper bound. Its complete declared list of columns. Each imported::Column has a local ID, additional objective cost, nonnegativequantity bounds, an integrality flag and coalesced (original_variable_id, coefficient) entries. IDs need only be unique within their subproblem. Entriesmay be signed or fractional. An omitted entry has coefficient zero. For every original variable declared by any imported subproblem, the interfaceadds the equality x = sum(coefficient * column_quantity) over all participatingimports. Several subproblems may contribute to the same original variable.Declared supports with no columns still imply zero contribution. Originalvariables outside all imported supports remain independent master variables.Original shared rows and original-variable bounds constrain these aggregatevalues. Routing networks continue to contribute their own ordinary shared-rowcoefficients. The objective includes both original-variable costs and each column's additionalcost. To supply the whole pattern cost in Column::cost, set the correspondingoriginal-variable costs to zero. If an original variable represents a nonlinearper-pattern feature, callers supply that feature's actual coefficient in eachcolumn; this interface does not discover or separate nonlinear cuts. The declared columns define this finite domain. Importing a subset of anexternal pricing problem does not establish completeness for that largerproblem. Every declared column is loaded immediately; this is not a dynamicpricing callback.

title: Finite column imports
heading: Solving and restricting snapshots

title: Finite column imports
heading: Extending a declared domain
text: Extending a declared domain node.solve_with_columns(subproblem_id, additional_columns, options) solves anew declared model containing the old and additional columns. IDs must be newwithin that existing subproblem, and entries must use its declared originalcoordinate support. Repeated extensions are supported; duplicate IDs andinvalid definitions are errors that leave the parent usable. Explicit with_variable_bounds, with_column_bounds, with_multiplicity,with_routing_multiplicity, with_row, with_presence_row,with_registered_cut_row, with_composite_cut_row,with_resource_knapsack_row and fix_routerestrictions survive the rebuild. They are replayed by original IDs andqualified column IDs, so a changed internal allocation does not retarget a fix.with_multiplicity addresses imported groups; with_routing_multiplicityaddresses total route use in a routing subproblem. fix_route(route_index, quantity)fixes additional integer copies of a registered routing path. Rebuilds preserveits physical arc path and quantity, subtract its contribution from every sharedrow and remaining route multiplicity, and retain its objective contribution.Fixed copies still count against group multiplicity and contribute their costsand original vectors. Ordinary low-level child snapshots obtained throughnode.node() are separate objects; only the import wrapper's explicitrestrictions are replayed by this extension operation. Use node.with_row(row, routing_coefficients, original_coefficients) to add ashared restriction. Original coefficients are (original_variable_id, value)pairs; generated imported-column IDs are rejected. Routing coefficients usemulti_pricing::RowCoefficients, with physical arc order and an optionalonce-per-route term. Omitted coordinates and routing families contribute zero.Coefficients must be finite and coalesced. The caller supplies a valid cut orbranch restriction. Original-coordinate links apply the row to new importedvectors automatically. Rebuilds replay the row and subtract any fixed routingcontribution, whether the row was added before or after fixing. node.with_presence_row(row, presence_coefficients, original_coefficients)couples nonlinear routing-event presence to original coordinates. It usesmulti_pricing::PresenceCoefficients, with event lists aligned to physicalarcs, and supports both pair-count and any-pair semantics. The originalpresence descriptor survives extension. Fixed routes contribute their exactpresence coefficient before preprocessing the rebuilt model; imported vectorscontribute through the specified original-coordinate coefficients. The import snapshot and multi-group session also exposewith_registered_cut_row(row, routing, original),with_composite_cut_row(row, routing, original) andwith_resource_knapsack_row(row, routing, original). These accept the sameregistered cut or resource-load descriptors as ordinary routing snapshots,plus coefficients on original imported coordinates. Composite rows sum everysupplied kernel, including repeated descriptors on one routing group. Resourcerows retain the routing adapter's monotone binary-grid load and <= requirements.Their descriptors survive source batches, phase-I recovery, domain extensionand tree descendants. Original-domain certificates may remain weak for thesekernels. A correct restricted LP does not establish certified optimality; completerouting enumeration can supply the finite-domain proof after external sourcesare complete. Rebuilds install all routing kernels before replayingfixed-route contributions or running preprocessing. Callers remain responsiblefor the validity of the supplied row. Adding columns can invalidate bounds, zero fixings and infeasibility deductionsmade from the previous finite domain. The implementation therefore retains theoriginal input definition, rebuilds the model, replays explicit restrictions andreruns preprocessing and routing pricing. It starts with unknown lower boundsand discards old certificates, smoothing, cached columns and derived bounds.Even a zero-time solve of the expanded domain cannot inherit a narrower-domaincertificate. The supplied options configure this fresh solve. An empty additionresumes the unchanged snapshot and preserves its valid bounds. This operation rebuilds and reloads the declared model; it is not an incrementalpricing callback or a claim that an external pricing problem is exhausted. Theoriginal definition is retained once and shared between snapshots for thispurpose. Callers obtain values through the returned output's new identity map. node.node() exposes the ordinary immutable snapshot for preprocessing, trees,additional shared rows and MIP. Use node.values(&output.master_values) to decodevalues returned by those operations on this snapshot's descendants. Root solvesrelax declared integrality; tree or MIP enforces it. Pure imports have a completecolumn domain immediately, so solve_enumerated_mip needs no enumeration step.

title: Finite column imports
heading: Numerical pricing requests
text: Numerical pricing requests session.pricing(options) optimizes the currently known restricted master andreturns ImportPricing. It disables finite-domain preprocessing, smoothing andenumeration so deductions from the known columns cannot become assumptionsabout future columns. A pricing point carries no bound or completion flag. point.costs() exports an ImportCosts objective: additional column cost plusper_column plus the sum of each original vector entry times its coordinateprice. The constant includes base and explicit multiplicity restrictions.point.reduced_cost(column) validates a proposed new, zero-lower-bound columnand evaluates its numerical reduced cost with the same reconstructed row maps.Original-coordinate objective costs enter through these duals; do not add thema second time. These are numerical search signals, not certified lower bounds. point.reduced_cost_bounds(column) returns an enclosure of that candidate'sexact-real reduced cost at the stored binary64 dual point. Exact expansionspreserve cancellation; directed intervals handle fractional underflow. Nonemeans arithmetic could not establish a finite enclosure; invalid candidatesremain errors. An upper endpoint below zero establishes a negative reduced costfor that candidate. A nonnegative lower endpoint establishes nonnegativity forthat candidate only. Neither result covers other columns or completes anexternal domain. Phase-I requests automatically omit original objective costs. Objective pricing fixes artificial quantities to zero before accepting duals.If the objective pass did not retain necessary routing paths, recovery obtainsfeasible paths from phase I and rebuilds their identities and original costs.A small finite artificial penalty therefore cannot by itself block an otherwisefeasible restricted-domain pricing request. A pricing request requires an optimal feasible restricted master. An empty orinfeasible restricted domain may need additional feasibility columns; the APIreturns an error rather than concluding that the external domain is infeasible.Numerical pricing requests publish no external-domain bound. Separate opt-incertificate requests are described below. Use the collection protocol to accept columns;only explicit enumeration completion permits the final declared-domain solve. For a restricted domain missing feasibility columns, usesession.feasibility_pricing(options). It minimizes artificial activity withall real objective costs zero, including imported columns, original coordinates,routing arcs and fixed route costs. The returned point haskind() == ImportPricingKind::Feasibility; restricted_violation() reportsnumerical artificial activity in the current restricted master. Positiveactivity does not prove the external domain infeasible, and zero activity doesnot complete that domain. ImportCosts.kind identifies the pricing objective. In feasibility mode,ignore additional column costs and minimize only per_column plus the vectorentries times coordinate prices. reduced_cost handles this distinctionautomatically. After generating feasibility columns, request ordinary objectiveprices to continue optimization. These phase-I signals are numerical; they donot constitute an exact Farkas certificate for an unknown domain. Time-limitedor unsolved augmented masters return an error instead of a stale pricing point.

title: Finite column imports
heading: Permitted column envelopes
text: Permitted column envelopes session.with_envelope(ColumnEnvelope { cost_lower, coordinates }) declaresrestrictions on every column in that imported group, including future columns.cost_lower bounds the additional Column.cost; each (original_id, Bounds)entry bounds one vector coordinate. Declare every coordinate in the group'ssupport exactly once. Omitted column entries mean zero. Known columns mustalready satisfy the declaration. Repeated envelopes intersect, preservingprevious restrictions. Collection and direct extension reject violations, and envelopes persist throughcompletion, snapshots and later extensions. A declaration is model input; itmust describe the intended domain. It is not inferred from the known columns. point.envelope_reduced_cost_bound() encloses the minimum reduced cost over thepermitted feature box and cost floor at the stored dual point. It relaxescorrelations, so it also covers unseen permitted columns. Objective pricinguses the additional-cost floor; phase-I pricing uses zero real cost. An adverseunbounded coordinate or missing cost floor can yield negative infinity. Nonemeans no envelope was declared or arithmetic could not establish a bound. Algebraic candidate queries may evaluate symbolic vectors outside the envelope;model acceptance still enforces it. This is useful for constructing the affineobjective intercept. An envelope reduced-cost bound alone does not establish afull-master bound, external feasibility or enumeration completion.

title: Finite column imports
heading: Certificates for open domains
text: Certificates for open domains session.objective_certificate(options) requests a conservative objective lowerbound over the retained finite imports, original routing domains, and everyfuture column permitted by this open group's envelope.session.feasibility_certificate(options) instead bounds the zero-real-costfeasibility model. Its strict positivity proves infeasibility for that declaredmodel. session.infeasibility_certificate(options) returns Some only whenthat strictly positive proof is available. Otherwise it returns None. ImportCertificate exposes kind(), lower_bound() and proves_infeasible().These requests are opt-in; ordinary pricing remains numerical. They do not marka collection complete or enable a final finite-domain solve while it is open. Publication requires coverage of future columns, valid dual signs and exactfixed-route reductions. Adverse residuals at unbounded original-variableendpoints, unsupported arithmetic or an adverse missing-column price withouta finite total multiplicity cap leave the bound unknown. Declared and explicitgroup multiplicity limits both apply. A zero total cap needs no envelope; anonnegative missing-column price needs no finite cap. Corrections use the fulltotal cap, which is conservative even when known copies already consume it. Bounds inferred by projecting only the known columns are excluded from thesecertificates: future vectors can invalidate those bounds. begin_import opens one group; begin_imports below opens several together.Unselected groups retain their declared finite domains.

title: Finite column imports
heading: Several open imported groups
text: Several open imported groups node.begin_imports(&[group_ids]) creates MultiImport over one shared model.Use with_envelope(group_id, envelope) for each selected group. Unknown orduplicate IDs are rejected. Empty selections are already complete. collect and collect_priced visit unfinished groups in the requested order,round-robin, under a shared deadline and batch budget. Every pricing requestsees all accepted columns from every group. ColumnBatch.complete completesonly the requested group. pending_groups() reports the remaining groups;solve is available only after all selected domains complete. Empty nonterminalbatches consume budget and cannot starve the other groups. Errors preserve theinput session, including batches accepted earlier in the failed call. The objective/feasibility/infeasibility certificate methods cover everyunfinished group at the shared dual point. Missing coverage for any such groupkeeps publication unknown. ImportCertificate::open_groups() identifies theunfinished domains covered by that certificate. Completed groups use theiractual finite columns, even if their envelopes were coarse. Once all selectedgroups complete, finite-domain projections may be used again. An empty selectionneeds no pricing callback; use its ordinary solved output for certificates.

title: Finite column imports
heading: Automatic pricing requests during collection
text: Automatic pricing requests during collection session.collect_priced(&limits, options, callback) runs a fresh restrictedphase-I request for each batch. Positive restricted artificial activity selectsfeasibility prices; zero selects ordinary objective prices. The callbackreceives &ImportPricing and the remaining time, with all previously acceptedcolumns visible through point.subproblem(). Both LP requests share the collection deadline and respect stricter LP timelimits. A batch/time limit returns a resumable session; the next call rebuildsprices for its accepted domain. Empty nonterminal batches consume the batchbudget. Invalid data or callback errors preserve the input session, with thesame external-side-effect caveat as ordinary collection. The callback returns ColumnBatch. Its completion flag still declares fullenumeration of the intended domain. Finding no negative reduced cost does notcomplete a session or authorize a bound. This driver automates feasibility andobjective pricing requests; it supplies no global pricing certificate. As withordinary collection, synchronous callbacks must cooperate with the remainingtime argument. For mixed routing/import models, all routing families must also complete theirenumeration before the MIP can claim full-domain coverage. MIP requires highs. This interface is currently Rust-only; CLI/Python input fields are unchanged.

title: Finite column imports
heading: Trees with open external groups
text: Trees with open external groups session.begin_tree() creates an immutable ImportTree. Calling it declaresthat every unseen column has quantity lower bound zero; register mandatorycolumns before starting. Tree callbacks reject new positive-lower-boundcolumns. This makes an exactly validated solution using known columns a validincumbent while external domains remain open. Call tree.run(&tree_options, &import_limits, callback) with ordinaryAssignmentTreeOptions and ImportOptions. The callback receives fresh phase-Ior objective prices for the current node. Original-variable, qualified-column,routing-multiplicity and physical-arc branches remain in the restriction journalwhen new patterns arrive. Accepted patterns are shared with siblings. A sourcecompletion flag must enumerate the group's entire intended domain, includingpatterns excluded by a node's aggregate restrictions; completion is shared withsiblings too. Open nodes use directed envelope certificates for objective pruning andinfeasibility. Missing or loose certificates keep the node open. An integralrestricted solution alone never closes it. Once every group completes, freshpreprocessing and the existing finite-domain tree, enumeration and optional MIPbecome available. No finite-parent proof survives opening a domain. The result contains tree, status, bound_mode, bound, incumbent, open_nodes andper-invocation node/batch/column counts. Resume with result.tree.run(...) aftera node, batch or time limit. Preserve the bound mode across resumptions.tree.solution() returns the best validated objective, physical routes andoriginal/qualified column values from the incumbent's own lineage. Newlyregistered optional columns can be absent from those stored values. Empty nonterminal batches visit the other unfinished groups. A full roundwithout additions or completion returns Incomplete with a reusable frontier.Callback errors or invalid batches preserve the input tree; external callbackside effects remain caller-owned. Both budgets share one deadline, andsynchronous callbacks must cooperate with the remaining-time argument. Open sessions also provide with_variable_bounds, with_column_bounds,with_multiplicity, with_routing_multiplicity, with_row,with_presence_row, with_registered_cut_row, with_composite_cut_row andwith_resource_knapsack_row. These immutable restrictions apply during pricing andsurvive future source batches. Original-coordinate links automatically carryadditive and nonlinear-row coupling to newly accepted vectors.

text:
P-step CVRP extension Documentation index baldes::extensions::pstep implements the compact continuous relaxation inProposition 1 of A p-step Formulation for the Capacitated Vehicle RoutingProblem, Dollevoet, Munari and Spliet. The extension is available without Cargo features. Solving requires animplementation of Baldes's LpMaster, such as Clp (--features clp). cargo build --release --features clp --bin baldes
./target/release/baldes pstep instances/cvrplib/P-n16-k8.vrp --p 2 --threads 4
./target/release/baldes pstep instances/cvrplib/P-n16-k8.vrp --p 3 --threads 4 --enumerate --json pstep.json
 Use baldes pstep --help for time, iteration and label limits. --enumeratechecks the bound against the complete column pool; use it on small cases.The JSON separates a converged full-model lp_bound from a potentiallynonconverged restricted_objective. A work-limit error cannot certify a bound.Neither output is an integer routing solution. The fleet is unlimited even ifthe CVRPLIB instance name or header specifies a conventional truck count. Rust callers can use Problem::from_instance on a parsed inputs::Instance.It preserves the input's distance rounding. Then callProblem::solve_column_generation with an empty LpMaster andColumnGenerationOptions; pricing.p and pricing.threads control the stepsize and CPU parallelism; pricing.method selects Auto (default),Enumeration, or Bucket. The older examples/pstep.rs illustrates full-poolconstruction, and examples/pstep_cvrp.rs produces CSV benchmark records. Create a Problem with customer demands, vehicle capacity and a directed costmatrix. Matrix indices are start depot 0, customers 1..=n, end depot n+1.For a conventional single-depot instance, copy depot-to-customer costs intorow 0 and customer-to-depot costs into column n+1. None means no arc.Customer demands must be strictly positive; capacity and supplied costs mustbe finite, with nonnegative costs. The model has an unlimited homogeneous fleet. Problem::enumerate builds the complete column pool for a supplied positivep. Every partial path is elementary and capacity feasible. Paths have exactlyp arcs, except those starting at the depot, which may be shorter. Empty depotroutes are omitted. At large p, the pool contains full routes and depotprefixes; flow conservation forces incomplete prefixes to zero. The compact prior-demand choices are zero for depot starts, maximum feasibleprior demand for depot ends, and both extremes for internal paths. Coincidentextremes are stored once. A junction customer's demand belongs to both adjacentpaths; the load coefficients account for this overlap. Formulation::entries exposes sparse columns in this row order: Rows Coefficient Sense / RHS 0..n Customer degree (1 at endpoints, 2 internally) = 2 n..2n Start +1, end -1 = 0 2n..3n Start d + q_i, end -(d + q(path)) >= 0 Formulation::into_master populates an empty LP backend with nonnegativecontinuous columns. Solve through the backend's status and time-limit API.An optimal solve gives the full p-step LP bound to solver tolerance. At p=1this has the single-commodity flow bound; at p>=n+1 it has the set-partitioningbound. Bounds need not increase at every successive p; the paper guaranteesnondecrease when p is replaced by an integer multiple. The reference enumerate implementation has combinatorial cost. Both columncount and search work are bounded by EnumerationOptions. Hitting a limitreturns an error instead of returning a restricted pool as a complete model.It is intended as an exact column-pool reference for small instances and small p. price_steps solves independent jobs for each start, end and prior-demandextreme. The default Auto method uses streaming elementary enumeration whenp<=6 and the dense prefix estimate 1+n+...+n^(p-1) is at most 100,000;otherwise it uses the core bucket-graph labeling engine. This is a boundedsize heuristic, not a prediction that one backend always wins. Capacity andmissing arcs prune enumeration further. Enumeration retains just the bestpath per job, so it does not build the full column pool. Both methods solvethe same exact pricing problem and enforce work/time limits. Use --pricing enumeration or --pricing bucket to compare a specific case;--enumerate remains the independent full-pool LP cross-check. --labelslimits generated labels for bucket pricing and attempted extensions forstreaming enumeration. JSON reports these separately as generated_labelsand enumerated_extensions, and records the requested and selected methods.Exceeding either budget aborts pricing without certifying convergence. For bucket pricing, hop count is an equalityresource, preventing artificial waiting from creating extra arcs. Capacity isdisposable: every load window has lower bound zero, so waiting never helps anda cheaper label using less capacity safely dominates. Reduced costs use actualcustomer demands, not any resource waiting. Customer startsrequire exactly p arcs; depot starts allow 1..p. The fixed endpoints and extrememake the reduced cost additive along arcs, including degree, endpoint and loadduals. Each returned path is replayed against the master coefficients. Workers share immutable instance costs and duals. Each owns its searchstorage and results. Results are merged in fixed job order and all threadsjoin before the main thread updates the LP. threads=1 runs the same pricingalgorithm, making serial/parallel results reproducible. Parallel overhead mayoutweigh the benefit on very small cases. The solver starts with degree artificials, uses exact pricing to complete phaseI, and then switches to travel costs. Convergence requires every pricing jobto finish without a negative reduced-cost step at the requested tolerance.Steps are deduplicated by node order and prior demand. LP columns are added inbatches. Restricted-master objectives are not full-model lower bounds untilpricing converges. Reported bounds are numerical, not independently certified. For p<=3 the path topology itself enforces elementarity. For p=4, a relaxedbucket solve is sufficient when its minimum is elementary. Otherwise, pricingpartitions by the first arc and forbids later returns to its head. Each resultingfour-arc path is elementary; every feasible elementary step belongs to onepartition. The relaxed minimum also bounds these partitions. Longer steps useexact cycle exclusion around bucket solves: a cyclic relaxed minimum branches onforbidding each arc of a detected cycle. Every elementary path lies in at leastone child; relaxed costs bound each child. This avoids the core's 15-elementlocal NG mask limit. It can still require exponential work for larger p.PricingOptions bounds total labels and bucket subproblems per endpoint job,as well as worker count and time. Exceeding a pricing limit returns an error. Time windows, cuts, integer solving and integration with Baldes'sbranch-and-price tree are not implemented here. For integeroptimization of this compact model, impose binary aggregate arc flows, asin equations (7)–(9); making extreme p-step columns binary is not equivalent.The exposed paths and coefficients provide the data needed for a separatearc-flow integrality implementation. Run node scripts/benchmark_pstep.mjs ./target/release/baldes from the repositoryroot to repeat the known-instance validation and serial/parallel timing checks.It writes raw JSON and CSV records under results/pstep-20261020/ and comparesevery bound with full column enumeration. Add --grid to run p=2,3,4 on all three bundled CVRPLIB instances, with fourworkers, 120 seconds per solve and five million labels per endpoint job. Gridrecords go under results/pstep-20261020/p234/. Reference enumeration is omittedfor the larger p=4 pools and A-n32-k5 at p=3, whose pool exceeds the CLI's columnlimit. Pricing stops are recorded explicitly, without a claimed LP bound. The validation runs gave these numerical bounds (four workers, developmentprofile). The normal CVRP column uses default root NG-route pricing; the integervalues were obtained separately with the normal tree solver. The A-n32-k5 integer solve used capacity cuts, rank-one cuts and aone-second HGS warm start before closing the gap at 784. Compare backends with node scripts/benchmark_pstep_pricing.mjs. Set PSTEP_RUNS,PSTEP_SECONDS, or PSTEP_THREADS to change repetitions, per-solve limits,or worker count. An optional binary path and output directory are accepted. title: EVRP implementation status
heading: EVRP implementation status
text: EVRP implementation status Documentation index baldes::extensions::evrp is the initial model and independent schedule replay layer.It supports deterministic directed travel with separate time, energy and cost,delivery capacity, customer service-start windows, repeat charging-stationvisits, and explicit partial charging with station-specific piecewise-linearcurves. Fixed-sequence charging optimization and reference bidirectional directpricing and a two-phase subpath prototype are available. Both feed the sameroute-based LP master and column-generation adapter. Charging curves map energy to cumulative time from empty. Charging from ato b takes T(b) - T(a); charge_for applies the inverse curve and caps atfull charge. Knots must start at zero and increase strictly in both coordinates.Non-concave charging profiles are accepted. Energy and time units are suppliedconsistently by callers. Problem::replay takes an explicit closed route with an amount charged pervisit and an initial departure time. The vehicle starts full. It reports everyarrival, service start, departure and arrival/departure energy, plus totaltravel cost and delivered load. Charging follows station service and mustfinish by closing; customers only require service start within their window.Waiting is allowed and consumes no energy. A route can cover a customer subset,but cannot repeat customers or contain intermediate depots. Comparisons usestrict floating-point bounds with no implicit tolerance. Travel costs must benonnegative; pricing reduced costs are not inputs to this validator. Replay checks feasibility of a supplied charging schedule, not optimalityof its charging decisions. Tariffs, charger congestion, regeneration, mixedvehicle compatibility and station insertion are not implemented.

title: EVRP implementation status
heading: Fixed stop sequence optimizer
text: Fixed stop sequence optimizer Problem::optimize_fixed_order(order, departure, ChargingOptions::default())chooses continuous partial charging amounts on a supplied sequence of customersand stations. It minimizes completion time. Travel cost is fixed by thatsequence, and charging has no separate monetary cost in the current model.Station visits may repeat; customer visits must be elementary. The algorithm propagates piecewise-affine earliest departure time as a functionof exact remaining energy. At a station, for cumulative charging time T andincoming time function F, it evaluatesT(x) + min { F(q) - T(q) : q <= x }. On each affine interval the minimum isattained at an endpoint or at q = x. All these candidates are generated;their lower envelope is split at domain endpoints and function intersections.The construction permits non-concave charging curves without an energy grid.Time-window waiting is another piecewise-affine operation. Every retained piecekeeps its predecessor and energy mapping for schedule reconstruction. The result distinguishes Optimal, Infeasible, WorkLimit, andNumericalFailure. Optimal is the optimizer's result in floating-pointarithmetic, not an interval-arithmetic certificate. Every returned schedulepasses independent strict replay. Reconstruction that fails replay reportsNumericalFailure, never Infeasible. The work budget counts generated piecesand envelope comparisons; reaching it yields no feasibility or optimality claim.The envelope implementation prioritizes a transparent reference algorithm overlarge-instance speed. Tests compare charging allocations against independent quarter-energy gridenumeration on tiny heterogeneous/non-concave instances whose optimum lies onthat grid, and check waiting, repeated stations, exact windows and work limits.These tests do not establish performance on published benchmarks.

title: EVRP implementation status
heading: Direct bidirectional pricing
text: Direct bidirectional pricing Problem::price_direct(duals, fleet_dual, departure, DirectOptions::default())prices elementary customer routes with repeatable station visits. The dualvector has one entry per location and must be zero at stations and depots.Reduced cost is travel cost minus customer duals minus one fleet dual. The bestreplay-validated route is returned even when its reduced cost is nonnegative.No subset-row cuts, ng relaxation or branching restrictions are accepted yet. The implementation uses forward earliest-departure functions F(e) andbackward latest-departure functions B(e) at exact departure energy e. Backwardfunctions exclude processing at the meeting node, already processed by theforward label. Internally backward times are negated to share lower-envelopecode. Backward extension undoes charging, station closing, service, customerwindows and travel in the appropriate order. At a station the core operationis max { B(y) - T(y) : y >= q } + T(q) - service, with station closing appliedto departure before charging is undone. Dominance conservatively requires equal visited-customer sets, no greaterreduced cost, no more used arcs and pointwise time dominance over the entireother function's domain. The function comparison covers domain gaps andinterior crossings; endpoint-only scalar tests are insufficient. Joins requirecompatible customer sets, capacity, total arc count and some common energywith F(e) <= B(e). Both directions retain energy mappings for reconstruction;every returned complete route passes strict schedule replay. This is an E1-inspired reference implementation of the coherent functionextension/dominance/join approach described byNafstad, Desaulniers and Stålhane (2025), Sections 3–4.The prefix/suffix affine-envelope construction is specific to Baldes's model;the paper's faster PWL algorithm, midpoint-by-time stopping, unreachable-customersets and acceleration techniques are not reproduced here. The current objectiveis travel cost, not the paper's separate route-duration extension. Pricing statuses are explicit: Bounded: all customer-serving routes with at most max_arcs travel arcswere covered. This does not certify that longer routes have no negative cost. Complete: that bound covers every relevant route, using customerelementarity when there are no stations, or a conservative depot-horizonbound when all available non-self travel times are strictly positive. WorkLimit / NumericalFailure: no pricing completeness claim. Any returnedincumbent remains independently replay-validated. Complete describes exhaustive model coverage in f64 arithmetic, not a rigorousreal-number reduced-cost certificate. No station-repeat bound is inferred fromzero-time travel. Nonnegative-cost self loops are omitted because they cannotimprove a schedule or customer coverage. Work/label limits and arc limits areconfigurable. Both directions currently grow to half the arc bound and comparecompatible label pairs; this prioritizes correctness evidence on tiny casesover large-instance speed. Tests compare minimum reduced costs to exhaustive stop-order enumeration withthe fixed-order optimizer, with dominance enabled and disabled. They also checkcapacity, customer elementarity, zero-time travel, work limits, bounded versusglobal coverage, and domain-interior dominance failures.

title: EVRP implementation status
heading: Two-phase subpath prototype
text: Two-phase subpath prototype Problem::price_subpaths(duals, fleet_dual, departure, SubpathOptions::default())uses the same objective, dual convention, route arc limit and completenessstatuses as direct pricing. Phase one generates elementary customer ordersbetween depot/station endpoints with no interior charging. It retains all suchorders fitting a full battery and load capacity, including direct charger-to-charger moves with no customers. max_subpaths caps this phase explicitly. Phase two composes these subpaths into complete routes. It propagates theentire continuous time/energy function through every constituent customer andendpoint, optimizes charging, and checks customer elementarity and capacity.It may prune a prefix only with equal customer history, no greater reduced cost,no more arcs and full function-domain dominance. Subpaths are never suppliedas master columns. Both backends return the same complete-route representationwith a replay-validated charging schedule. The decomposition is inspired byJacquillat and Lo, v3 (2026).The prototype deliberately retains distinct phase-one orders and carries fullcharging functions in phase two. It does not implement the paper's compressedresource vectors, two-sided subpath domination, adaptive ng relaxation or cuts.Thus it does not assume that scalar forward domination can replace the paper'sdomination requirements. Keeping the full prefix state makes composition anexplicit dynamic program under this static model; the paper's speedups havenot been reproduced. Tests compare both backends with exhaustive route-order evaluation, under thesame data, duals and arc bounds, with dominance enabled and disabled. Fixturesinclude heterogeneous/non-concave charging, repeated stations, and a route withtwo consecutive charging stops in both directions. Global versus boundedcoverage and phase-one/phase-two work limits have separate checks.
