text: Source mapping and implementation C++ source Rust module Behavior ip_solver.h, src/ipm/ip_solver.cpp model.rs, solver/ Standard form, homogeneous self-dual Mehrotra loop, upper-bound elimination, adaptive regularization, predictor/corrector and centrality corrections, recovery hipo_ldlt.h factor/mod.rs, sparse_solver.rs::HiPOLDLT Block ordering, symbolic fill, fundamental supernodes, elimination forest, frontal assembly, child Schur updates, restricted 1x1/2x2 Bunch–Kaufman pivots, sign-preserving small-pivot regularization, refinement normal_eq_ldlt.h sparse_solver.rs::NormalEqLDLT SPD normal equations A D⁻¹ Aᵀ + Rd, followed by primal recovery sparse_solver.h sparse_solver.rs::SparseSolver Backend dispatch and structural fill estimate Eigen sparse/dense plumbing matrix.rs, factor/mod.rs Owned sparse CSC input and factors stored as sparse columns; dense arrays only for individual fronts and Schur updates The augmented matrix is [-(theta + Rp), Aᵀ; A, Rd]. The ordering preservesthe primal/dual boundary, and fundamental supernodes cannot cross it. Frontsare processed in increasing elimination order, a valid child-before-parentorder, and child Schur buffers are released after parent assembly. Child updatesstore only the lower triangle, packed by row; parents assemble that trianglewithout copying an unused upper half.Sparse augmented factors may use an up-looking row-update path when theprimal block has at least twice as many variables as rows and symbolic L hasat most 32 off-diagonal entries per system variable on average. This pathexpects negative primal and positive dual pivots; small, non-finite or wronglysigned pivots retry the existing pivoted multifrontal factorization. OriginalKKT refinement remains enabled. Sparse factor columns use contiguous CSC valuesand share an immutable pattern across numerical refactors and clones. Numeric pivot swaps are composed with the symbolic permutation and applied torows of previously assembled factor columns. Iterative refinement uses|b - Kx| / (|b| + |K||x|) with at most two correction solves. Deliberate differences from C++: Ordering keeps the independent diagonal primal block in natural order.Eliminating these vertices cannot connect other primal vertices, so buildinga primal column-intersection graph cannot reduce fill. The dual Schur graphuses deterministic exact minimum degree with explicit graph updates,rather than the shared C++ approximate minimum degree quotient graph.Complete remaining graphs are emitted directly; dense intersection graphsuse packed adjacency (at most 32 MiB), while sparse or larger graphs retaintree sets. Those graph representations produce the same ordering. Primalreordering preserves structural fill but can change floating-point sums. The normal-equations path uses this crate's multifrontal factorization,rather than the external C++ supernodal implementation. Its fixed CSC patternand row-to-column source positions are cached; refactors accumulate valuesdirectly without duplicate triplets or repeated sorting. The comparison backends LDLT, SUPERNOODAL, and FRONTAL from the siblinglinear_system directory are not separately ported or aliased to HiPO. Fixed variables are eliminated. Free variables, upper-only bounds, shiftedbounds, zero columns, mixed senses, objective offsets and row dual signsare tracked explicitly through recovery. Complementarity includes the upper-bound slack/multiplier product. Successchecks primal feasibility as well as dual feasibility and gap. Centrality corrections are added to the current Newton direction insteadof overwriting it. The homogeneous Schur denominator uses its equivalentpositive quadratic form to avoid subtractive cancellation. A singular 2x2 pivot returns a numerical error instead of replacing onlyits determinant, which would be inconsistent with the stored D block. Ruiz equilibration is implemented and enabled by default (five passes).The C++ header declares scaling routines, but its optimization loop doesnot invoke them. Set scaling_iterations: 0 to disable scaling. The internal objective is normalized after equilibration. Dual recovery anddual/gap checks undo objective scaling, retaining tolerances in originalunits. Wide upper bounds start with feasible slacks and unit complementarityproducts, avoiding a large artificial residual from bounds such as 1e12. A regularized least-squares starting estimate reduces initial row and dualresiduals before positive shifts for the HSD variables. Finite upper boundsretain unit complementarity. Unsafe estimates, empty systems and very tightbounds retain the unit initializer. This adds one factorization and two solvesper eligible LP; it is not a warm start from the previous CG solve. The restricted master selects this solver with --master ipm; the API is alsousable independently. Performance parity with theC++ solver and large-instance robustness have not been established; there isno parallel factorization, relaxed supernode amalgamation or nested dissection.

text: Column elimination model reductions Measured on 2026-10-21. title: Column elimination model reductions
heading: Reference audit
text: Reference audit The reference implementation was inspected atvrptwdecisiondiagram.cppand vrptwddsolver.cpp. Reference mechanism Result in this implementation generateNewStateRelaxation, compileNgRoute: load, time and ng visit memory Added capacity-indexed states with two-customer ng memory for bounded integer-demand CVRP cases; general instances use forward resource bounds and layered states. Initial time bucketing remains unimplemented. addNode, separateRoute: state reuse and outgoing exact-feasibility checks Added exact state sharing by location, complete visited set and bitwise load/time; new states filter every outgoing action. fixArcs: forward/backward reduced-cost distances and an incumbent cutoff Not copied into the continuous LP mode. An integer incumbent cutoff does not justify setting every positive fractional use of an expensive arc to zero. findMergeNodesReducedCost: relaxed dominance merging above a reduced-cost threshold Not enabled; this differs from sharing equal exact states and can weaken the relaxation. Flow-model dual starts; Lagrangian/subgradient solving; RCC/SRC separation and primal heuristics Remain separate future work. These require additional backend/state mapping or a stronger, explicitly different optimization mode. The candidate also physically removes unreachable nodes and disabled arcs,so dead rows/columns no longer enter subsequent LPs or occupy persistentdiagram budgets. Every retained internal node lies on a root-to-sink path.

title: Column elimination model reductions
heading: Preservation rules
text: Preservation rules Forward load/time labels are independent minima, not a claim that one pathattains both. A transition is removed only if an optimistic label alreadyviolates a resource constraint. A reverse connectivity pass removes deadregions. The same floating-point operation order as route replay is used foreach forward resource update; no triangle inequality is assumed. Exact refinement uses the complete visited set, including zero-demandcustomers. Bitwise active-resource matching avoids approximate state merging.Arrival time is omitted only when every deadline is infinite and a monotoneupper-bound calculation proves all elementary route times remain finite.The preflight accounts for reused states and filtered successors, so arefinement that does not fit leaves the diagram untouched. The capacity initial model is used automatically for at least 20 customerswhen demands are positive bounded integers and every window upper bound isinfinite. Demand GCD scaling is exact. Scaled capacity must be at most 4n,and conservative dense state/arc estimates must fit the requested budgets.Zero/fractional demand or finite windows use the general construction.
